    62→        shell: bash
    63→        env:
    64→          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
    65→        run: |
    66→          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"

    81→          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
    82→            --name "e2e-triage" \
    83→            --dir "triage-plans" || {

    95→          prompt: |

    97→
    98→            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
    99→            1. mise run fmt

1→name: E2E Triage
     2→
     3→on:
     4→  workflow_dispatch:
     5→    inputs:
     6→      run_url:
     7→        description: GitHub Actions run URL to triage
     8→        required: true
     9→        type: string
    10→      sha:
    11→        description: Commit SHA (auto-detected from run if omitted)
    12→        required: false
    13→        type: string
    14→      failed_agents:
    15→        description: Comma-separated list of failed agents (auto-detected from run if omitted)
    16→        required: false
    17→        type: string
    18→      slack_channel:
    19→        description: Slack channel ID for the originating thread
    20→        required: false
    21→        type: string
    22→      slack_thread_ts:
    23→        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
    24→        required: false
    25→        type: string
    26→      rerun:
    27→        description: 'Re-run failing tests locally to detect flaky (costs API tokens)'
    28→        required: false
    29→        type: boolean
    30→        default: false
    31→
    32→permissions:
    33→  actions: read
    34→  contents: read
    35→  id-token: write
    36→
    37→concurrency:
    38→  group: e2e-triage-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
    39→  cancel-in-progress: true
    40→
    41→jobs:
    42→  setup:
    43→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    44→    env:
    45→      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
    46→    outputs:
    47→      agents_csv: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents_csv }}
    48→      run_url: ${{ steps.set.outputs.run_url }}
    49→      sha: ${{ steps.set.outputs.sha }}
    50→      slack_channel: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_channel }}
    51→      slack_thread_ts: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    52→    steps:
    53→      - name: Checkout repository
    54→        uses: actions/checkout@v6
    55→        with:
    56→          fetch-depth: 1
    57→          sparse-checkout: scripts
    58→
    59→      - name: Validate payload
    60→        id: set
    61→        shell: bash
    62→        env:
    63→          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    64→          REPO_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
    65→          RUN_URL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
    66→          SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.sha }}
    67→          FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
    68→          SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
    69→          SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    70→        run: |
    71→          set -euo pipefail
    72→
    73→          run_url="$RUN_URL_INPUT"
    74→          sha="${SHA_INPUT:-}"
    75→          slack_channel="${SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT:-}"
    76→          slack_thread_ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT:-}"
    77→
    78→          # Normalize thread_ts — re-insert dot if stripped (always 6 decimal places)
    79→          # Slack ts format is "seconds.microseconds" e.g. "1482960137.003543"
    80→          # See: https://api.slack.com/messaging/retrieving
    81→          if [ -n "$slack_thread_ts" ] && ! echo "$slack_thread_ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
    82→            slack_thread_ts="$(echo "$slack_thread_ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
    83→          fi
    84→
    85→          # Derive missing values from run URL via GitHub API
    86→          if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
    87→            run_id=$(echo "$run_url" | grep -oE '/runs/[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
    88→            if [ -z "$run_id" ]; then
    89→              echo "Could not extract run ID from run_url: $run_url" >&2
    90→              exit 1
    91→            fi
    92→            run_data=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$REPO_NAME" --json headSha,jobs)
    93→            if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
    94→              sha=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -r '.headSha')
    95→            fi
    96→            if [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
    97→              # Extract agent names from failed job names like "e2e (gemini-cli)"
    98→              agents_csv=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -r '[.jobs[]
    99→                | select(.conclusion == "failure")
   100→                | (.name | (try capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)").agent catch null))
   101→                | select(. != null)
   102→              ] | join(", ")')
   103→            fi
   104→          fi
   105→
   106→          if [ -n "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
   107→            agents_csv="$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT"
   108→          fi
   109→
   110→          if [ -z "$run_url" ]; then
   111→            echo "run_url is required" >&2
   112→            exit 1
   113→          fi
   114→          if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
   115→            echo "sha is required" >&2
   116→            exit 1
   117→          fi
   118→          if [ -z "$agents_csv" ]; then
   119→            echo "agents is required (provide failed_agents input or ensure failed job names contain '(agent-name)')" >&2
   120→            exit 1
   121→          fi
   122→
   123→          echo "run_url=$run_url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   124→          echo "sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   125→          echo "slack_channel=$slack_channel" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   126→          echo "slack_thread_ts=$slack_thread_ts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   127→          echo "agents_csv=$agents_csv" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

   216→            1. Triage findings (per-test findings blocks + summary table from the skill)
   217→            2. A "## Fix Plan" section with specific code changes for each actionable finding
   218→
   219→            When done, call ExitPlanMode.
   220→          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
   221→          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Read,Grep,Glob,Write,EnterPlanMode,ExitPlanMode'"
   222→          display_report: false
   223→          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
   224→
   225→      - name: Run triage (with re-runs)
   226→        id: triage_rerun
   227→        if: inputs.rerun == true
   228→        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
   229→        env:
   230→          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
   231→          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
   232→          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
   233→          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
   234→          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   235→        with:
   236→          prompt: |
   237→            Enter plan mode, then read and follow the full E2E triage procedure from .claude/skills/e2e/triage-ci.md.
   238→
   239→            Inputs:
   240→            - CI run URL: ${{ env.RUN_URL }}
   241→            - Failed agents: ${{ env.FAILED_AGENTS }}
   242→            - SHA: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.sha }}
   243→
   244→            Analyze ALL failed agents together -- failures may share a common root cause.
   245→
   246→            Write ALL output to the plan file -- both the triage findings report and the fix plan. Structure it as:
   247→            1. Triage findings (per-test findings blocks + summary table from the skill)
   248→            2. A "## Fix Plan" section with specific code changes for each actionable finding
   249→
   250→            When done, call ExitPlanMode.
   251→          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
   252→          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Read,Grep,Glob,Write,EnterPlanMode,ExitPlanMode,Bash(mise:*),Bash(scripts:*)'"
   253→          display_report: false
   254→          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
   255→
   256→      - name: Resolve triage outcome
   257→        id: triage
   258→        if: always()
   259→        shell: bash
   260→        env:
   261→          ANALYSIS_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.triage_analysis.outcome }}
   262→          ANALYSIS_EXEC: ${{ steps.triage_analysis.outputs.execution_file }}
   263→          RERUN_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.triage_rerun.outcome }}
   264→          RERUN_EXEC: ${{ steps.triage_rerun.outputs.execution_file }}
   265→        run: |
   266→          outcome="${ANALYSIS_OUTCOME:-skipped}"
   267→          exec_file="${ANALYSIS_EXEC}"
   268→          if [ "$outcome" = "skipped" ]; then
   269→            outcome="${RERUN_OUTCOME:-skipped}"
   270→            exec_file="${RERUN_EXEC}"
   271→          fi
   272→          echo "outcome=$outcome" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   273→          echo "execution_file=$exec_file" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   274→
   275→      - name: Extract triage output
   276→        id: triage_output
   277→        if: always() && steps.triage.outputs.execution_file != ''
   278→        shell: bash
   279→        env:
   280→          EXECUTION_FILE: ${{ steps.triage.outputs.execution_file }}
   281→          TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e-triage-artifacts/triage.md
   282→          PLAN_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e-triage-artifacts/plan.md
   283→        run: |
   284→          set -euo pipefail
   285→          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE")"
   286→
   287→          # Try to extract from plan file on disk (plan mode writes here)
   288→          plan_src=$(find /home/runner/.claude/plans -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -1)
   289→          if [ -n "$plan_src" ] && [ -s "$plan_src" ]; then
   290→            combined="$(cat "$plan_src")"
   291→          else
   292→            # Fallback: extract assistant text from execution JSON
   293→            combined=$(jq -r '[.[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]
   294→              | select(.type == "text") | .text] | join("\n")' "$EXECUTION_FILE")
   295→          fi
   296→
   297→          # Split on "## Fix Plan" header
   298→          if echo "$combined" | grep -q "^## Fix Plan"; then
   299→            echo "$combined" | sed '/^## Fix Plan/,$d' > "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"
   300→            echo "$combined" | sed -n '/^## Fix Plan/,$p' > "$PLAN_FILE"
   301→          else
   302→            echo "$combined" > "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"
   303→            echo "$combined" > "$PLAN_FILE"
   304→          fi
   305→
   306→          # Copy execution JSON to artifacts for debugging
   307→          cp "$EXECUTION_FILE" "$(dirname "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE")/execution.json" 2>/dev/null || true
   308→
   309→      - name: Write job summary
   310→        if: always() && steps.triage_output.outcome == 'success'
   311→        shell: bash
   312→        env:
   313→          TRIAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e-triage-artifacts/triage.md
   314→          PLAN_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/e2e-triage-artifacts/plan.md
   315→        run: |
   316→          set -euo pipefail
   317→          {
   318→            echo "# E2E Triage: ${FAILED_AGENTS}"
   319→            echo ""
   320→            if [ -s "$TRIAGE_FILE" ]; then
   321→              cat "$TRIAGE_FILE"
   322→            else
   323→              echo "_No triage findings._"
   324→            fi
   325→            echo ""
   326→            echo "---"
   327→            echo ""
   328→            if [ -s "$PLAN_FILE" ]; then
   329→              cat "$PLAN_FILE"
   330→            else
   331→              echo "_No fix plan._"
   332→            fi
   333→          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
   334→
   335→      - name: Post triage result
   336→        if: ${{ always() && (steps.triage.outputs.outcome == 'success' || steps.triage.outputs.outcome == 'failure') && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
   337→        shell: bash
   338→        env:
   339→          TRIAGE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.triage.outputs.outcome }}
   340→          TRIAGE_OUTPUT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.triage_output.outcome }}
   341→          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
   342→          SUMMARY_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
   343→        run: |
   344→          set -euo pipefail
   345→
   346→          if [ "$TRIAGE_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
   347→            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E triage failed — <${SUMMARY_URL}|view run>"
   348→            exit 0
   349→          fi
   350→
   351→          if [ "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
   352→            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E triage completed but output extraction failed — <${SUMMARY_URL}|view run>"
   353→            exit 0
   354→          fi
   355→
   356→          # Construct Fix It URL
   357→          encoded_run_url="$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse, os; print(urllib.parse.quote(os.environ['RUN_URL'], safe=''))")"
   358→          encoded_agents="$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse, os; print(urllib.parse.quote(os.environ['FAILED_AGENTS'], safe=''))")"
   359→          fix_url="https://e2e-triage.entireio.workers.dev/fix?triage_run_id=${TRIAGE_RUN_ID}&run_url=${encoded_run_url}&failed_agents=${encoded_agents}&slack_channel=${SLACK_CHANNEL}&slack_thread_ts=${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
   360→
   361→          # Block Kit payload with button
   362→          payload="$(jq -n \
   363→            --arg summary_url "$SUMMARY_URL" \
   364→            --arg fix_url "$fix_url" \
   365→            '{
   366→              text: "E2E triage complete",
   367→              blocks: [
   368→                {
   369→                  type: "section",
   370→                  text: {
   371→                    type: "mrkdwn",
   372→                    text: (":white_check_mark: E2E triage complete — <" + $summary_url + "|view results>\nClick *Fix It* to apply the plan and create a draft PR.")
   373→                  }
   374→                },
   375→                {
   376→                  type: "actions",
   377→                  elements: [
   378→                    {
   379→                      type: "button",
   380→                      text: { type: "plain_text", text: "Fix It" },
   381→                      url: $fix_url,
   382→                      style: "primary"
   383→                    }
   384→                  ]
   385→                }
   386→              ]
   387→            }')"
   388→
   389→          scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
   390→
   391→      - name: Upload triage output
   392→        if: always()
   393→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
   394→        with:
   395→          name: e2e-triage
   396→          path: e2e-triage-artifacts/
   397→          retention-days: 7

1→name: E2E Fix
     2→
     3→on:
     4→  workflow_dispatch:
     5→    inputs:
     6→      triage_run_id:
     7→        description: Run ID of the triage workflow (for downloading plan artifacts)
     8→        required: true
     9→        type: string
    10→      run_url:
    11→        description: Original failed E2E run URL
    12→        required: true
    13→        type: string
    14→      failed_agents:
    15→        description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix
    16→        required: true
    17→        type: string
    18→      slack_channel:
    19→        description: Slack channel ID for thread replies
    20→        required: false
    21→        type: string
    22→      slack_thread_ts:
    23→        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
    24→        required: false
    25→        type: string
    26→
    27→permissions:
    28→  actions: read
    29→  contents: write
    30→  pull-requests: write
    31→  id-token: write
    32→
    33→concurrency:
    34→  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
    35→  cancel-in-progress: true
    36→
    37→jobs:
    38→  fix:
    39→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    40→    timeout-minutes: 30
    41→    env:
    42→      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
    43→      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
    44→      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    45→    steps:
    46→      - name: Checkout repository
    47→        uses: actions/checkout@v6
    48→        with:
    49→          fetch-depth: 0
    50→
    51→      - name: Normalize Slack thread_ts
    52→        shell: bash
    53→        run: |
    54→          ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
    55→          if [ -n "$ts" ] && ! echo "$ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
    56→            ts="$(echo "$ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
    57→            echo "SLACK_THREAD_TS=$ts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    58→          fi
    59→
    60→      - name: Post fix started
    61→        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
    62→        shell: bash
    63→        env:
    64→          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
    65→        run: |
    66→          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"
    67→
    68→      - name: Setup mise
    69→        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
    70→
    71→      - name: Download plan artifacts
    72→        env:
    73→          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    74→          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
    75→        shell: bash
    76→        run: |
    77→          set -euo pipefail
    78→
    79→          mkdir -p triage-plans
    80→
    81→          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
    82→            --name "e2e-triage" \
    83→            --dir "triage-plans" || {
    84→            echo "error: no triage artifact found for run $TRIAGE_RUN_ID" >&2
    85→            exit 1
    86→          }
    87→
    88→          echo "Downloaded plans:"
    89→          find triage-plans -name '*.md' -type f
    90→
    91→      - name: Apply fixes
    92→        id: fix
    93→        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
    94→        with:
    95→          prompt: |
    96→            Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).
    97→
    98→            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
    99→            1. mise run fmt
   100→            2. mise run lint
   101→            3. mise run test:e2e:canary
   102→
   103→            If verification passes, create a git branch fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}, commit all changes,
   104→            push, and create a draft PR with a summary of what was fixed.
   105→
   106→            If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.
   107→          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
   108→          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"
   109→
   110→      - name: Post success to Slack
   111→        if: success() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
   112→        shell: bash
   113→        env:
   114→          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
   115→          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
   116→          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
   117→        run: |
   118→          set -euo pipefail
   119→
   120→          pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"
   121→
   122→          if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
   123→            payload="$(jq -n \
   124→              --arg pr_url "$pr_url" \
   125→              '{
   126→                text: (":review: E2E fix applied: " + $pr_url),
   127→                reply_broadcast: true,
   128→                unfurl_links: true
   129→              }')"
   130→            scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
   131→          else
   132→            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E fix complete but no PR was created — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
   133→          fi
   134→
   135→      - name: Post failure to Slack
   136→        if: failure() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
   137→        shell: bash
   138→        env:
   139→          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
   140→        run: |
   141→          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
   142→

1→name: E2E Tests
     2→
     3→on:

     5→    inputs:
     6→      agent:

     8→        required: false
     9→        type: choice
    10→        options:
    11→          - ''
    12→          - claude-code
    13→          - opencode
    14→          - gemini-cli
    15→          - factoryai-droid
    16→          - cursor-cli
    17→          - copilot-cli
    18→          - roger-roger
    19→  push:
    20→    branches:
    21→      - main
    22→
    23→permissions:
    24→  actions: read
    25→  contents: read
    26→

    28→concurrency:
    29→  group: e2e-tests
    30→  cancel-in-progress: true
    31→
    32→jobs:
    33→  # Build the matrix dynamically so workflow_dispatch can select a single agent.
    34→  matrix-setup:
    35→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    36→    outputs:
    37→      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
    38→    steps:
    39→      - id: set

    46→          fi

    49→    needs: matrix-setup

    54→      matrix:

    56→
    57→    steps:

    61→      - name: Setup mise

    77→          esac

   102→          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}

   107→
   108→      - name: Upload artifacts

   112→          name: e2e-artifacts-${{ matrix.agent }}

   115→
   116→  notify-slack:

   143→                  }
   144→                },
   145→                {
   146→                  "type": "context",
   147→                  "elements": [
   148→                    {
   149→                      "type": "mrkdwn",
   150→                      "text": "Commit: <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}|${{ github.sha }}> by ${{ github.actor }}"

   153→                }
   154→              ]
   155→            }

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -euo pipefail
     3→
     4→# Post a message to a Slack thread using the chat.postMessage API.
     5→# Requires SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_CHANNEL, and SLACK_THREAD_TS env vars.
     6→#
     7→# Usage:
     8→#   post-slack-message.sh "plain text message"
     9→#   post-slack-message.sh --payload '{"text":"fallback","blocks":[...]}'
    10→#
    11→# With --payload, channel and thread_ts are injected automatically.
    12→
    13→if [ "$1" = "--payload" ]; then
    14→  payload="$(echo "$2" | jq \
    15→    --arg channel "$SLACK_CHANNEL" \
    16→    --arg thread_ts "$SLACK_THREAD_TS" \
    17→    '. + {channel: $channel, thread_ts: $thread_ts}')"
    18→else
    19→  text="${1:?message is required}"
    20→  payload="$(jq -n \
    21→    --arg channel "$SLACK_CHANNEL" \
    22→    --arg thread_ts "$SLACK_THREAD_TS" \
    23→    --arg text "$text" \
    24→    '{channel: $channel, thread_ts: $thread_ts, text: $text}')"
    25→fi
    26→
    27→if ! response="$(curl -fsS https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
    28→  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" \
    29→  -H 'Content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
    30→  --data "$payload")"; then
    31→  echo "warning: slack notification failed" >&2
    32→  exit 0
    33→fi
    34→
    35→if ! jq -e '.ok == true' >/dev/null <<<"$response"; then
    36→  error="$(jq -r '.error // "unknown"' <<<"$response")"
    37→  echo "warning: slack notification returned non-ok response: $error" >&2
    38→  echo "warning: full response: $response" >&2
    39→fi
    40→

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -euo pipefail
     3→
     4→# Post a message to a Slack thread using the chat.postMessage API.
     5→# Requires SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_CHANNEL, and SLACK_THREAD_TS env vars.
     6→#
     7→# Usage:
     8→#   post-slack-message.sh "plain text message"
     9→#   post-slack-message.sh --payload '{"text":"fallback","blocks":[...]}'
    10→#
    11→# With --payload, channel and thread_ts are injected automatically.
    12→
    13→if [ "$1" = "--payload" ]; then
    14→  payload="$(echo "$2" | jq \
    15→    --arg channel "$SLACK_CHANNEL" \
    16→    --arg thread_ts "$SLACK_THREAD_TS" \
    17→    '. + {channel: $channel, thread_ts: $thread_ts}')"
    18→else
    19→  text="${1:?message is required}"
    20→  payload="$(jq -n \
    21→    --arg channel "$SLACK_CHANNEL" \
    22→    --arg thread_ts "$SLACK_THREAD_TS" \
    23→    --arg text "$text" \
    24→    '{channel: $channel, thread_ts: $thread_ts, text: $text}')"
    25→fi
    26→
    27→if ! response="$(curl -fsS https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
    28→  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" \
    29→  -H 'Content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
    30→  --data "$payload")"; then
    31→  echo "warning: slack notification failed" >&2
    32→  exit 0
    33→fi
    34→
    35→if ! jq -e '.ok == true' >/dev/null <<<"$response"; then
    36→  error="$(jq -r '.error // "unknown"' <<<"$response")"
    37→  echo "warning: slack notification returned non-ok response: $error" >&2
    38→  echo "warning: full response: $response" >&2
    39→fi
    40→

1→# E2E Triage CI
     2→
     3→Triage E2E test failures with **re-run verification**. Analyzes artifacts and re-runs failing tests locally to distinguish flaky from real bugs. Produces a findings report with classifications -- does NOT apply fixes. Does deep analysis of the code.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Step L1: Parse User Input
     8→
     9→The user provides one or more of:
    10→- **Test name(s)** -- e.g., `TestInteractiveMultiStep`
    11→- **`--agent <agent>`** -- optional, defaults to all agents that previously failed
    12→- **A local artifact path** -- skip straight to analysis of existing artifacts
    13→- **CI run reference** -- triggers artifact download instead of local re-runs:
    14→  - `latest CI run` / `latest` -- most recent failed E2E run on main
    15→  - A GitHub Actions run ID (numeric, e.g., `12345678`)
    16→  - A GitHub Actions run URL
    17→
    18→**CI artifact download:** When a CI run reference is provided, download artifacts using:
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh <latest | RUN_ID | RUN_URL>
    22→```
    23→
    24→The script outputs the absolute artifact path as its **last line of stdout** -- capture that and use it as the artifact path for analysis. After downloading, **skip Steps L2-L5** (local re-runs) and go straight to **Shared Analysis** (Step 1), since we're analyzing CI artifacts, not running tests locally.
    25→
    26→**Cost warning:** Real E2E tests consume API tokens. Before running, confirm with the user unless they provided specific test names (implying intent to run).
    27→
    28→## Step L2: First Run
    29→
    30→```bash
    31→mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> <TestName>
    32→```
    33→
    34→Capture the artifact directory from the `artifacts: <path>` output line.
    35→
    36→## Step L3: Re-run on Failure
    37→
    38→If the test **passes** on first run: report as passing, done for this test.
    39→
    40→If the test **fails**: run a **second time** with the same parameters.
    41→
    42→## Step L4: Tiebreaker (if needed)
    43→
    44→If results are **split** (1 pass, 1 fail): run a **third time** as tiebreaker.
    45→
    46→## Step L5: Collect Results
    47→
    48→For each test+agent pair, record: `(test, agent, run_1_result, run_2_result, [run_3_result])`
    49→
    50→Proceed to **Shared Analysis** (Step 1 below).
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→## Shared Analysis & Classification
    55→
    56→### Step 1: Analyze Each Failure
    57→
    58→For each failure, follow the **Debugging Workflow** in `.claude/skills/e2e/debug.md` (steps 2-5: console.log -> test source -> entire.log -> deep dive). Collect:
    59→- What the agent actually did (from console.log)
    60→- What was expected (from test source)
    61→- CLI-level errors or anomalies (from entire.log)
    62→- Repo/checkpoint state (from git-log.txt, git-tree.txt, checkpoint-metadata/)
    63→
    64→### Step 2: Classify Each Failure
    65→
    66→Use **re-run results as the primary signal**, supplemented by artifact analysis.
    67→
    68→#### Re-run signals (strongest):
    69→
    70→| Original | Re-run 1 | Re-run 2 | Classification |
    71→|----------|----------|----------|----------------|
    72→| FAIL | FAIL (same error) | FAIL (same error) | **real-bug** OR **flaky (test-bug)** -- see below |
    73→| FAIL | PASS | PASS | **flaky** |
    74→| FAIL | PASS | FAIL | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    75→| FAIL | FAIL | PASS | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    76→| FAIL | FAIL (different error) | FAIL (different error) | **needs deeper analysis** -- examine artifacts |
    77→
    78→**Important: Consistent failures can still be `flaky` (test-bug).** When all re-runs fail, check *where* the root cause is:
    79→- Root cause in `cmd/entire/cli/` -> **real-bug** (product code is broken)
    80→- Root cause in `e2e/` (test infra, test helpers, tmux setup, env propagation) -> **flaky (test-bug)** -- the CLI works fine, the test is broken
    81→
    82→#### Strong `real-bug` signals (root cause must be in `cmd/entire/cli/`, not `e2e/`):
    83→
    84→- `entire.log` contains `"level":"ERROR"` or panic/stack traces from CLI code
    85→- Checkpoint metadata structurally corrupt (malformed JSON, missing `checkpoint_id`/`strategy`)
    86→- Session state file missing or malformed when expected
    87→- Hooks did not fire at all (no `hook invoked` log entries)
    88→- Shadow/metadata branch has wrong tree structure
    89→- Same test fails across 3+ agents with same non-timeout symptom
    90→- Error references CLI code (panic in `cmd/entire/cli/`)
    91→
    92→**Key question:** Is the bug in `cmd/entire/cli/` (product code) or in `e2e/` (test code)? Only the former is a `real-bug`.
    93→
    94→#### Strong `flaky` signals (unless overridden by real-bug):
    95→
    96→**Agent behavior (non-deterministic):**
    97→- `signal: killed` (timeout)
    98→- `context deadline exceeded` or `WaitForCheckpoint.*exceeded deadline`
    99→- Agent asked for confirmation instead of acting
   100→- Agent created file at wrong path / wrong name
   101→- Agent produced no output
   102→- Agent committed when it shouldn't have (or vice versa)
   103→- Duration near timeout limit
   104→
   105→**Test-bug (consistent failure, but root cause is in `e2e/` not `cmd/entire/cli/`):**
   106→- Agent "Not logged in" / auth errors -> test env setup doesn't propagate auth credentials
   107→- Env vars not propagated to agent session -> tmux/test harness bug
   108→- Error references test code (`e2e/`) not CLI code (`cmd/entire/cli/`)
   109→- Test helper logic errors (wrong assertions, bad globs, incorrect expected values)
   110→- Consistent failure BUT root cause traced to `e2e/` code, not `cmd/entire/cli/`
   111→- Test setup/teardown issues (missing git config, temp dir cleanup, port conflicts)
   112→
   113→#### Ambiguous cases:
   114→
   115→Read `entire.log` carefully:
   116→- If hooks fired correctly and metadata is valid -> lean **flaky**
   117→- If hooks fired but produced wrong results -> lean **real-bug**
   118→
   119→### Step 3: Cross-Agent Correlation
   120→
   121→Before reporting, check correlations using re-run data:
   122→- Same test fails for 3+ agents, all re-runs also fail -> strong **real-bug**
   123→- Same test fails for multiple agents, but re-runs pass -> **flaky** (shared prompt issue)
   124→- One agent fails consistently, others pass -> agent-specific issue (still **real-bug** if re-runs confirm)
   125→
   126→### Step 4: Present Findings Report
   127→
   128→For each test+agent pair, print a findings block:
   129→
   130→```
   131→## <TestName> (<agent>) -- <classification>
   132→
   133→**Re-run results:** original=FAIL, rerun1=PASS, rerun2=PASS
   134→**Evidence:**
   135→- <1-2 sentence summary of what went wrong>
   136→- <key artifact evidence: entire.log excerpt, console.log excerpt, etc.>
   137→```
   138→
   139→For `flaky` failures, include proposed fix description:
   140→
   141→```
   142→**Proposed fix:** <description>
   143→  - File: <path to test file or e2e infrastructure file>
   144→  - Change: <what will be modified>
   145→```
   146→
   147→Common flaky fixes:
   148→- Agent asked for confirmation -> append "Do not ask for confirmation" to prompt
   149→- Agent wrote to wrong path -> be more explicit about paths in prompt
   150→- Agent committed when shouldn't -> add "Do not commit" to prompt
   151→- Checkpoint wait timeout -> increase timeout argument
   152→- Agent timeout (signal: killed) -> increase per-test timeout, simplify prompt
   153→- Auth/env not propagated -> fix test harness env setup in `e2e/` code
   154→- Test helper bug (wrong assertion, bad glob) -> fix test helper in `e2e/`
   155→- tmux session setup issue -> fix `NewTmuxSession` or session config in `e2e/`
   156→
   157→For `real-bug` failures, include root cause analysis:
   158→
   159→```
   160→**Root cause analysis:**
   161→  - Component: <hooks | session | checkpoint | strategy | agent>
   162→  - Suspected location: <file:function>
   163→  - Description: <what's wrong and why>
   164→  - Proposed fix: <what code change would address it>
   165→```
   166→
   167→### Step 5: Summary
   168→
   169→Print a summary table (classification only, no "Action Taken"):
   170→```
   171→| Test | Agent(s) | Re-runs | Classification |
   172→|------|----------|---------|----------------|
   173→| TestFoo | claude-code | FAIL/PASS/PASS | flaky |
   174→| TestBar | all agents | FAIL/FAIL/FAIL | real-bug |
   175→| TestBaz | opencode | FAIL/PASS/FAIL | flaky (non-deterministic) |
   176→```
   177→

After downloading, **skip Steps L2-L5** (local re-runs) and go straight to **Shared Analysis** (Step 1), since we're analyzing CI artifacts, not running tests locally.
    25→
    26→**Cost warning:** Real E2E tests consume API tokens. Before running, confirm with the user unless they provided specific test names (implying intent to run).
    27→

    29→
    30→```bash
    31→mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> <TestName>
    32→```
    33→
    34→Capture the artifact directory from the `artifacts: <path>` output line.
    35→
    36→## Step L3: Re-run on Failure
    37→
    38→If the test **passes** on first run: report as passing, done for this test.
    39→
    40→If the test **fails**: run a **second time** with the same parameters.
    41→
    42→## Step L4: Tiebreaker (if needed)
    43→
    44→If results are **split** (1 pass, 1 fail): run a **third time** as tiebreaker.
    45→

    47→
    48→For each test+agent pair, record: `(test, agent, run_1_result, run_2_result, [run_3_result])`

    54→## Shared Analysis & Classification
    55→
    56→### Step 1: Analyze Each Failure
    57→
    58→For each failure, follow the **Debugging Workflow** in `.claude/skills/e2e/debug.md` (steps 2-5: console.log -> test source -> entire.log -> deep dive). Collect:
    59→- What the agent actually did (from console.log)
    60→- What was expected (from test source)
    61→- CLI-level errors or anomalies (from entire.log)
    62→- Repo/checkpoint state (from git-log.txt, git-tree.txt, checkpoint-metadata/)
    63→
    64→### Step 2: Classify Each Failure
    65→
    66→Use **re-run results as the primary signal**, supplemented by artifact analysis.
    67→

    69→
    70→| Original | Re-run 1 | Re-run 2 | Classification |
    71→|----------|----------|----------|----------------|
    72→| FAIL | FAIL (same error) | FAIL (same error) | **real-bug** OR **flaky (test-bug)** -- see below |
    73→| FAIL | PASS | PASS | **flaky** |
    74→| FAIL | PASS | FAIL | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    75→| FAIL | FAIL | PASS | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    76→| FAIL | FAIL (different error) | FAIL (different error) | **needs deeper analysis** -- examine artifacts |
    77→
    78→**Important: Consistent failures can still be `flaky` (test-bug).** When all re-runs fail, check *where* the root cause is:
    79→- Root cause in `cmd/entire/cli/` -> **real-bug** (product code is broken)
    80→- Root cause in `e2e/` (test infra, test helpers, tmux setup, env propagation) -> **flaky (test-bug)** -- the CLI works fine, the test is broken
    81→
    82→#### Strong `real-bug` signals (root cause must be in `cmd/entire/cli/`, not `e2e/`):
    83→
    84→- `entire.log` contains `"level":"ERROR"` or panic/stack traces from CLI code
    85→- Checkpoint metadata structurally corrupt (malformed JSON, missing `checkpoint_id`/`strategy`)
    86→- Session state file missing or malformed when expected
    87→- Hooks did not fire at all (no `hook invoked` log entries)
    88→- Shadow/metadata branch has wrong tree structure
    89→- Same test fails across 3+ agents with same non-timeout symptom
    90→- Error references CLI code (panic in `cmd/entire/cli/`)
    91→
    92→**Key question:** Is the bug in `cmd/entire/cli/` (product code) or in `e2e/` (test code)? Only the former is a `real-bug`.
    93→
    94→#### Strong `flaky` signals (unless overridden by real-bug):
    95→
    96→**Agent behavior (non-deterministic):**
    97→- `signal: killed` (timeout)
    98→- `context deadline exceeded` or `WaitForCheckpoint.*exceeded deadline`
    99→- Agent asked for confirmation instead of acting
   100→- Agent created file at wrong path / wrong name
   101→- Agent produced no output
   102→- Agent committed when it shouldn't have (or vice versa)
   103→- Duration near timeout limit
   104→
   105→**Test-bug (consistent failure, but root cause is in `e2e/` not `cmd/entire/cli/`):**
   106→- Agent "Not logged in" / auth errors -> test env setup doesn't propagate auth credentials
   107→- Env vars not propagated to agent session -> tmux/test harness bug
   108→- Error references test code (`e2e/`) not CLI code (`cmd/entire/cli/`)
   109→- Test helper logic errors (wrong assertions, bad globs, incorrect expected values)
   110→- Consistent failure BUT root cause traced to `e2e/` code, not `cmd/entire/cli/`
   111→- Test setup/teardown issues (missing git config, temp dir cleanup, port conflicts)
   112→
   113→#### Ambiguous cases:
   114→
   115→Read `entire.log` carefully:
   116→- If hooks fired correctly and metadata is valid -> lean **flaky**
   117→- If hooks fired but produced wrong results -> lean **real-bug**
   118→
   119→### Step 3: Cross-Agent Correlation
   120→
   121→Before reporting, check correlations using re-run data:
   122→- Same test fails for 3+ agents, all re-runs also fail -> strong **real-bug**
   123→- Same test fails for multiple agents, but re-runs pass -> **flaky** (shared prompt issue)
   124→- One agent fails consistently, others pass -> agent-specific issue (still **real-bug** if re-runs confirm)
   125→
   126→### Step 4: Present Findings Report
   127→
   128→For each test+agent pair, print a findings block:
   129→
   130→```
   131→## <TestName> (<agent>) -- <classification>
   132→
   133→**Re-run results:** original=FAIL, rerun1=PASS, rerun2=PASS
   134→**Evidence:**
   135→- <1-2 sentence summary of what went wrong>
   136→- <key artifact evidence: entire.log excerpt, console.log excerpt, etc.>
   137→```
   138→
   139→For `flaky` failures, include proposed fix description:
   140→
   141→```
   142→**Proposed fix:** <description>
   143→  - File: <path to test file or e2e infrastructure file>
   144→  - Change: <what will be modified>
   145→```
   146→
   147→Common flaky fixes:
   148→- Agent asked for confirmation -> append "Do not ask for confirmation" to prompt
   149→- Agent wrote to wrong path -> be more explicit about paths in prompt
   150→- Agent committed when shouldn't -> add "Do not commit" to prompt
   151→- Checkpoint wait timeout -> increase timeout argument
   152→- Agent timeout (signal: killed) -> increase per-test timeout, simplify prompt
   153→- Auth/env not propagated -> fix test harness env setup in `e2e/` code
   154→- Test helper bug (wrong assertion, bad glob) -> fix test helper in `e2e/`
   155→- tmux session setup issue -> fix `NewTmuxSession` or session config in `e2e/`
   156→
   157→For `real-bug` failures, include root cause analysis:
   158→
   159→```
   160→**Root cause analysis:**
   161→  - Component: <hooks | session | checkpoint | strategy | agent>
   162→  - Suspected location: <file:function>
   163→  - Description: <what's wrong and why>
   164→  - Proposed fix: <what code change would address it>
   165→```
   166→
   167→### Step 5: Summary
   168→
   169→Print a summary table (classification only, no "Action Taken"):
   170→```
   171→| Test | Agent(s) | Re-runs | Classification |
   172→|------|----------|---------|----------------|
   173→| TestFoo | claude-code | FAIL/PASS/PASS | flaky |
   174→| TestBar | all agents | FAIL/FAIL/FAIL | real-bug |
   175→| TestBaz | opencode | FAIL/PASS/FAIL | flaky (non-deterministic) |
   176→```

## Summary: E2E Fix and Triage Workflows

Based on my thorough analysis of the GitHub Action workflows and supporting scripts, here's the complete picture:

### **1. The Full Workflow Architecture**

The E2E failure handling consists of **three connected workflows**:

#### **A. E2E Tests Workflow** (`e2e.yml`)
- **Triggers:** Manual dispatch or pushes to `main`
- **What it does:** Runs E2E tests against 7 agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Roger Roger)
- **On failure:** Posts a Slack notification to `#e2e-failed` channel with failed agent names

#### **B. E2E Triage Workflow** (`e2e-triage.yml`)
- **Triggers:** Manual workflow dispatch (lines 4-30 show inputs for: `run_url`, `sha`, `failed_agents`, `slack_channel`, `slack_thread_ts`, and `rerun` flag)
- **Key features:**
  - **Step 1 (Setup job):** Validates and normalizes inputs, extracts SHA and agent names from failed CI run via GitHub API
  - **Slack thread normalization:** Fixes Slack thread_ts format (adds dot between seconds.microseconds)
  - **Step 2 (Triage job):** Downloads E2E artifacts (40 files per agent, retention 7 days) using `download-e2e-artifacts.sh`
  - **Parallel analysis paths:**
    - **Without rerun** (default): Analyzes downloaded CI artifacts directly
    - **With rerun** (optional): Installs agent CLIs, re-runs failing tests locally (2-3 times each to detect flakiness)
  - **Claude Code action:** Invokes Claude Code with plan mode enabled to perform deep triage analysis
  - **Output:** Generates two markdown files in artifacts:
    - `triage.md` - Findings report with test-by-test analysis and classification (real-bug vs flaky)
    - `plan.md` - "## Fix Plan" section with specific code changes
  - **Slack notification:** Posts success message with a "Fix It" button that links to the e2e-fix workflow

#### **C. E2E Fix Workflow** (`e2e-fix.yml`)
- **Triggers:** Manual workflow dispatch via the "Fix It" button (or direct trigger with parameters)
- **Inputs:** `triage_run_id`, `run_url`, `failed_agents`, `slack_channel`, `slack_thread_ts`
- **Key sequence:**
  1. Normalize Slack thread_ts (add dot if stripped)
  2. Post "fixing in progress" message to Slack thread
  3. Download triage artifacts (plan.md and triage.md from triage workflow)
  4. **Claude Code applies fixes** - executes exactly as specified in the plan:
     - Reads `triage-plans/plan.md` and `triage-plans/triage.md` for context
     - Applies all fixes
     - Runs verification (lines 99-101):
       ```
       1. mise run fmt
       2. mise run lint
       3. mise run test:e2e:canary
       ```
     - Creates branch `fix/e2e-<run_id>`, commits changes, pushes, and creates draft PR
     - **Retries if verification fails** - Claude attempts to fix lint/format errors
  5. **Validation success:** Slack notification with PR link
  6. **Validation failure:** Slack notification with failure URL

---

### **2. Whether It Runs the Failing E2E Test After Fix**

**YES - The workflow runs verification tests, but NOT the original failing E2E test.**

Instead, it runs:
- `mise run fmt` - Code formatting verification
- `mise run lint` - Linting verification  
- `mise run test:e2e:canary` - **The Vogon (deterministic fake agent) E2E test suite** (line 101)

The canary uses a fake agent to exercise the entire E2E pipeline without making real API calls, which is faster and cheaper. This verifies that:
- The CLI plumbing works (sessions, checkpoints, git operations)
- Test infrastructure isn't broken
- No regressions in core flow

**Note:** The canary does NOT re-run the actual failing test with the real agent that originally failed. That would require real API calls and cost tokens.

---

### **3. How It Validates the Fix Works**

**Multi-stage validation:**

1. **Formatting check:** `mise run fmt` - ensures code meets Go formatting standards
2. **Linting check:** `mise run lint` - ensures code meets golangci-lint standards
3. **CLI functional test:** `mise run test:e2e:canary` - runs the full CLI session workflow with Vogon (fake agent)

**If any stage fails:**
- Claude Code is instructed to: "Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors" (line 106)
- It attempts to diagnose and fix the issues
- Creates a NEW commit (not amending - per Claude Code standards)
- Re-verifies all stages

**Success criteria:**
- All format/lint checks pass
- Canary E2E test passes
- Draft PR created successfully

---

### **4. Retry/Verification Logic**

**In the Fix workflow:**

- **Line 106:** "If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors."
- **Lines 110-133:** On success, posts PR link to Slack
- **Lines 135-141:** On failure, posts error message to Slack with run URL for debugging

**Important design decision:**
- The workflow does NOT automatically re-run the original failing E2E test (with the real agent that failed)
- Instead, it validates via the canary (Vogon deterministic test)
- The assumption: if the fix passes canary + linting + formatting, it should work for real agents
- The real E2E test validation happens when the PR is merged or manually triggered

**Concurrency control (line 33-35):**
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
Prevents multiple fix attempts on the same failed run from running simultaneously.

---

1. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.github/workflows/e2e-fix.yml`** - Main fix workflow
2. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml`** - Triage workflow that feeds into fix
3. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.github/workflows/e2e.yml`** - Original E2E test workflow
4. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/scripts/post-slack-message.sh`** - Slack notification helper
5. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh`** - Artifact download script
6. **`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.claude/skills/e2e/triage-ci.md`** - Triage procedure documentation

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me create a comprehensive summary document:

## E2E Triage & Fix Pipeline - Complete Analysis

Based on my thorough review of all workflow files, scripts, and supporting documentation, here's the full architecture of the E2E triage-to-fix pipeline:

---

### 1. FAILURE DETECTION & SLACK NOTIFICATION

**Trigger:** E2E tests fail on `main` branch
- Location: `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (lines 19-20) - runs on every `push` to `main`
- Multiple agents tested in parallel (Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Factory AI Droid, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Roger Roger)

**Slack Notification** (lines 116-156 in `e2e.yml`):
- Job: `notify-slack` runs only if `e2e-tests` fails AND event is `push`
- Uses `slackapi/slack-github-action` with incoming webhook (`E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` secret)
- Posts to public channel (via webhook) with:
  - Red circle icon + "E2E Tests Failed" header
  - Failed agent names extracted via regex: `capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)")`
  - Link to GitHub Actions run
  - Commit hash and author

---

### 2. TRIAGE WORKFLOW DISPATCH

**Manual Trigger:** User clicks "Run workflow" button in GitHub UI or it can be triggered programmatically

**Workflow File:** `.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml`

**Inputs** (lines 4-30):
- `run_url` (required): GitHub Actions run URL to triage
- `sha` (optional): Commit SHA - auto-detected from run if omitted
- `failed_agents` (optional): Comma-separated list - auto-detected from run if omitted
- `slack_channel` (optional): Slack channel ID for thread replies
- `slack_thread_ts` (optional): Slack thread timestamp (dot may be stripped)
- `rerun` (optional, boolean): Re-run failing tests locally to detect flaky (costs tokens)

**Job Structure:**

#### Job 1: `setup` (lines 42-137)
Runs once, validates payload and extracts missing values from GitHub API:

1. **Validates payload** (lines 60-127):
   - Extracts run ID from `run_url`
   - Calls `gh run view` API to get commit SHA and jobs
   - Extracts failed agent names from job names using regex: `\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)`
   - **Thread normalization** (lines 78-83): Re-inserts dot into `slack_thread_ts` if stripped (format: "seconds.microseconds")

2. **Slack notification - triage starting** (lines 129-137):
   - Calls `scripts/post-slack-message.sh` if Slack config provided
   - Posts hourglass emoji + link to triage run to thread

name: E2E Fix

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      triage_run_id:
        description: Run ID of the triage workflow (for downloading plan artifacts)
        required: true
        type: string
      run_url:
        description: Original failed E2E run URL
        required: true
        type: string
      failed_agents:
        description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix
        required: true
        type: string
      slack_channel:
        description: Slack channel ID for thread replies
        required: false
        type: string
      slack_thread_ts:
        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Normalize Slack thread_ts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
          if [ -n "$ts" ] && ! echo "$ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
            ts="$(echo "$ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
            echo "SLACK_THREAD_TS=$ts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Post fix started
        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

      - name: Download plan artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p triage-plans

          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
            --name "e2e-triage" \
            --dir "triage-plans" || {
            echo "error: no triage artifact found for run $TRIAGE_RUN_ID" >&2
            exit 1
          }

          echo "Downloaded plans:"
          find triage-plans -name '*.md' -type f

      - name: Apply fixes
        id: fix
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).

            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            If verification passes, create a git branch fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}, commit all changes,
            push, and create a draft PR with a summary of what was fixed.

            If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Post success to Slack
        if: success() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"

          if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
            payload="$(jq -n \
              --arg pr_url "$pr_url" \
              '{
                text: (":review: E2E fix applied: " + $pr_url),
                reply_broadcast: true,
                unfurl_links: true
              }')"
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
          else
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E fix complete but no PR was created — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
          fi

      - name: Post failure to Slack
        if: failure() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"

name: E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agent:
        description: 'Run a single agent (leave empty for all)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        options:
          - ''
          - claude-code
          - opencode
          - gemini-cli
          - factoryai-droid
          - cursor-cli
          - copilot-cli
          - roger-roger
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

# Concurrency: only one E2E job runs at a time
concurrency:
  group: e2e-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Build the matrix dynamically so workflow_dispatch can select a single agent.
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
    steps:
      - id: set
        run: |
          input="${{ github.event.inputs.agent }}"
          if [ -n "$input" ]; then
            echo "agents=[\"$input\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'agents=["claude-code","opencode","gemini-cli","factoryai-droid","cursor-cli","copilot-cli","roger-roger"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  e2e-tests:
    needs: matrix-setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLI
        run: |
          case "${{ matrix.agent }}" in
            claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
            opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
            gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
            cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
            factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
            copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot  ;;
            roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise (see mise.toml)
          esac
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Verify roger-roger agent
        if: matrix.agent == 'roger-roger'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Verifying roger-roger binaries on PATH..."
          command -v roger-roger
          command -v entire-agent-roger-roger

      - name: Bootstrap agent
        if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap

      - name: Run E2E Tests
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT: ${{ matrix.agent == 'gemini-cli' && '6' || matrix.agent == 'factoryai-droid' && '1' || '' }}
        run: mise run test:e2e --agent ${{ matrix.agent }} ${{ matrix.agent == 'roger-roger' && 'TestExternalAgent' || '' }}

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts-${{ matrix.agent }}
          path: e2e/artifacts/
          retention-days: 7

  notify-slack:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [e2e-tests]
    if: ${{ always() && needs.e2e-tests.result == 'failure' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
    steps:
      - name: Get failed agents
        id: failed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/jobs \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name | capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)") | .agent] | join(", ")')
          echo "agents=$failed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Notify Slack of E2E failure
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@91efab103c0de0a537f72a35f6b8cda0ee76bf0a # v2.1.1
        with:
          webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          webhook-type: incoming-webhook
          payload: |
            {
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {

content.text:
The `test:e2e` command from e2e.yml runs `mise run test:e2e --agent <agent>`. Since it's not in mise.toml, it's likely a mise file-task or defined in a config I haven't found. But for the workflow design, the key command is clear: `mise run test:e2e --agent <agent>`.

Now I have enough context to design the plan. Here is the detailed implementation design.

---

## Implementation Plan: E2E Verification After Fix

### Architecture Decision: Separate Jobs

The verification must be a **separate job** (not steps in the `fix` job) for these reasons:

1. **Matrix support**: The failing agents need to run in parallel via a matrix strategy, which requires a separate job.
2. **Isolation**: Each agent needs its own runner with its own CLI installation and API keys.
3. **Clean checkout**: The verify job must check out the fix branch that was pushed by the `fix` job, not the original main branch.
4. **Timeout independence**: The fix job has a 30-minute timeout; verification needs its own timeout (e.g., 40 minutes per agent).

### Overall Workflow Structure (3 jobs)

```
fix  -->  verify (matrix: per-agent, runs 2x each)  -->  notify
```

- **fix**: Apply fixes, create branch/PR. No Slack success/failure messages (moved to notify).
- **verify**: Matrix job across failed agents. Runs E2E tests twice per agent on the fix branch.
- **notify**: Aggregates results from fix + verify, posts final Slack message.

### Detailed Changes to `e2e-fix.yml`

#### 1. Add `matrix-setup` job (between `fix` and `verify`)

This job converts the comma-separated `failed_agents` input into a JSON array for the matrix. It needs to run after `fix` succeeds because there is no point verifying if the fix failed.

```yaml
matrix-setup:
  needs: fix
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  outputs:
    agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
  steps:
    - id: set
      shell: bash
      env:
        FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
      run: |
        # Convert "claude-code, gemini-cli" to ["claude-code","gemini-cli"]
        agents_json=$(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
        echo "agents=$agents_json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

#### 2. Add `verify` job

This is the core addition. Key design choices:

- **Runs on the fix branch**: Uses `ref: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}` in checkout.
- **Two sequential test runs**: A loop `for run in 1 2; do ... done` that runs the full E2E suite twice. Both must pass. This catches flaky false-positives.
- **Same agent installation/bootstrap as e2e.yml**: Copy the install agent CLI step, bootstrap step, and secrets exactly from `e2e.yml`.
- **Concurrency limits**: Same `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` logic as `e2e.yml`.
- **roger-roger handling**: Same `if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'` guard on bootstrap.
- **Artifact upload**: Upload artifacts from each run for debugging.

```yaml
verify:
  needs: [fix, matrix-setup]
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 45
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false
    matrix:
      agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}
  steps:
    - name: Checkout fix branch
      uses: actions/checkout@v6
      with:
        ref: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}

    - name: Setup mise
      uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

    - name: Install system dependencies
      run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

    - name: Install agent CLI
      run: |
        case "${{ matrix.agent }}" in
          claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
          opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
          gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
          cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
          factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
          copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot  ;;
          roger-roger) ;;
        esac
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

    - name: Verify roger-roger agent
      if: matrix.agent == 'roger-roger'
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        command -v roger-roger
        command -v entire-agent-roger-roger

    - name: Bootstrap agent
      if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
        CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
        FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
        COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap

    - name: Run E2E verification (2 passes)
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
        CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
        FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
        COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT: ${{ matrix.agent == 'gemini-cli' && '6' || matrix.agent == 'factoryai-droid' && '1' || '' }}
      run: |
        for run in 1 2; do
          echo "=== Verification run $run/2 ==="
          mise run test:e2e --agent ${{ matrix.agent }} ${{ matrix.agent == 'roger-roger' && 'TestExternalAgent' || '' }}

Restructure the workflow from 1 job to 4 jobs:

fix  →  matrix-setup  →  verify (matrix: per-agent, 2x runs)  →  notify

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why run tests twice?** A single passing run after a fix doesn't distinguish between "the fix works" and "the test is flaky and happened to pass." Running twice catches the case where a flaky test masks an incomplete fix. This is the same principle the triage workflow uses when detecting flakiness — if results differ across runs, the test is non-deterministic.

**Why a separate `notify` job?** GitHub Actions `needs` + `if: always()` is the standard pattern for "run regardless of upstream outcome but with access to their results." Moving Slack notifications to a dedicated final job ensures they always fire and can report the combined fix + verification status.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Normalize Slack thread_ts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
          if [ -n "$ts" ] && ! echo "$ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
            ts="$(echo "$ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
            echo "SLACK_THREAD_TS=$ts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Post fix started
        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

      - name: Download plan artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p triage-plans

          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
            --name "e2e-triage" \
            --dir "triage-plans" || {
            echo "error: no triage artifact found for run $TRIAGE_RUN_ID" >&2
            exit 1
          }

          echo "Downloaded plans:"
          find triage-plans -name '*.md' -type f

      - name: Apply fixes
        id: fix
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).

            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            If verification passes, create a git branch fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}, commit all changes,
            push, and create a draft PR with a summary of what was fixed.

            If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Post success to Slack
        if: success() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"

          if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
            payload="$(jq -n \
              --arg pr_url "$pr_url" \
              '{
                text: (":review: E2E fix applied: " + $pr_url),
                reply_broadcast: true,
                unfurl_links: true
              }')"
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
          else
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E fix complete but no PR was created — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
          fi

      - name: Post failure to Slack
        if: failure() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"

Good point. Let me rethink the architecture. If verification fails, the most useful thing is to give Claude Code another shot with the failure context — since it's already in the same session and knows what it just fixed.

The cleanest way to do this in GitHub Actions is to keep everything in a **single job** with sequential steps:

1. Apply fixes (Claude Code)
2. Install agents + run E2E tests 2x
3. If tests fail → save failure output → invoke Claude Code again with failure context
4. Re-run E2E tests 2x
5. Create PR only after verification passes (or after best-effort on attempt 2)

This avoids the complexity of multi-job retry coordination and lets the retry Claude Code invocation see what went wrong.
