name: E2E Fix

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      triage_run_id:
        description: Run ID of the triage workflow (for downloading plan artifacts)
        required: true
        type: string
      run_url:
        description: Original failed E2E run URL
        required: true
        type: string
      failed_agents:
        description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix
        required: true
        type: string
      slack_channel:
        description: Slack channel ID for thread replies
        required: false
        type: string
      slack_thread_ts:
        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Normalize Slack thread_ts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
          if [ -n "$ts" ] && ! echo "$ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
            ts="$(echo "$ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
            echo "SLACK_THREAD_TS=$ts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Post fix started
        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

      - name: Download plan artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p triage-plans

          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
            --name "e2e-triage" \
            --dir "triage-plans" || {
            echo "error: no triage artifact found for run $TRIAGE_RUN_ID" >&2
            exit 1
          }

          echo "Downloaded plans:"
          find triage-plans -name '*.md' -type f

      - name: Apply fixes
        id: fix
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).

            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.

            Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet — E2E verification will happen in a later step.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLIs
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
        run: |
          for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
            case "$agent" in
              claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
              opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
              gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
              cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
              factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
              copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot ;;
              roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise
            esac
          done
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Bootstrap agents
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Skip bootstrap if only roger-roger
          agents=$(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' | grep -v '^roger-roger$' || true)
          if [ -n "$agents" ]; then
            go run ./e2e/bootstrap
          fi

      - name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 1)
        id: verify1
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          failed=""
          for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
            limit=""
            test_filter=""
            case "$agent" in
              gemini-cli) limit="6" ;;
              factoryai-droid) limit="1" ;;
              roger-roger) test_filter="TestExternalAgent" ;;
            esac
            export E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT="$limit"

            for run in 1 2; do
              echo "=== $agent: verification run $run/2 ==="
              if ! mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" $test_filter 2>&1 | tee -a e2e-verify-output.txt; then
                failed="$failed $agent(run$run)"
                echo "=== $agent: run $run FAILED ==="
                break
              fi
              echo "=== $agent: run $run passed ==="
            done
          done

          if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
            echo "FAILED:$failed" >> e2e-verify-output.txt
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Retry fix with failure context
        id: fix2
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            The previous E2E fix was applied but the E2E tests still fail.
            Read the test failure output in e2e-verify-output.txt.

            Also read the original triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md and fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md for context.

            Diagnose why the tests are still failing and apply additional fixes. After fixing, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 2)
        id: verify2
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          failed=""
          for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
            limit=""
            test_filter=""
            case "$agent" in
              gemini-cli) limit="6" ;;
              factoryai-droid) limit="1" ;;
              roger-roger) test_filter="TestExternalAgent" ;;
            esac
            export E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT="$limit"

            for run in 1 2; do
              echo "=== $agent: verification run $run/2 (attempt 2) ==="
              if ! mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" $test_filter 2>&1 | tee -a e2e-verify-output-2.txt; then
                failed="$failed $agent(run$run)"
                echo "=== $agent: run $run FAILED ==="
                break
              fi
              echo "=== $agent: run $run passed ==="
            done
          done

          if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
            echo "FAILED:$failed" >> e2e-verify-output-2.txt
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Create fix PR
        id: create_pr
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'success' || steps.verify2.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          ORIGINAL_RUN_URL: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
          VERIFY1_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          attempt="1"
          if [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
            attempt="2"
          fi

          git checkout -b "$FIX_BRANCH"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "$(cat <<COMMIT_EOF
          fix: resolve E2E test failures

          Automated fix applied by E2E fix workflow.
          Original failure: ${ORIGINAL_RUN_URL}

          Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
          COMMIT_EOF
          )"
          git push -u origin "$FIX_BRANCH"

          gh pr create --draft \
            --title "fix: resolve E2E test failures" \
            --body "$(cat <<PR_EOF
          ## Summary
          Automated fix for E2E test failures.

          - Original failure: ${ORIGINAL_RUN_URL}
          - Failed agents: ${FAILED_AGENTS}
          - Fix verified: E2E tests passed 2/2 runs (attempt $attempt)
          - Triage run: ${TRIAGE_RUN_URL}
          PR_EOF
          )"

      - name: Post result to Slack
        if: always() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          FIX_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.fix.outcome }}
          VERIFY1_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}
          VERIFY2_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify2.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [ "$FIX_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed to apply — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
            exit 0
          fi

          if [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" = "success" ] || [ "$VERIFY2_OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"
            attempt="1"
            [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" != "success" ] && attempt="2"

            if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
              payload="$(jq -n --arg pr_url "$pr_url" --arg attempt "$attempt" '{
                text: (":white_check_mark: E2E fix verified (" + $attempt + "/2 attempts, 2/2 test passes): " + $pr_url),
                reply_broadcast: true,
                unfurl_links: true
              }')"
              scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
            else
              scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E fix verified but no PR created — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
            fi
          else
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed verification after 2 attempts — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
          fi

      - name: Upload verification artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: e2e-fix-verification
          path: |
            e2e/artifacts/
            e2e-verify-output*.txt
          retention-days: 7

name: E2E Fix

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      triage_run_id:
        description: Run ID of the triage workflow (for downloading plan artifacts)
        required: true
        type: string
      run_url:
        description: Original failed E2E run URL
        required: true
        type: string
      failed_agents:
        description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix
        required: true
        type: string
      slack_channel:
        description: Slack channel ID for thread replies
        required: false
        type: string
      slack_thread_ts:
        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: e2e-fix-${{ inputs.run_url || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Normalize Slack thread_ts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS}"
          if [ -n "$ts" ] && ! echo "$ts" | grep -q '\.'; then
            ts="$(echo "$ts" | sed 's/\(.*\)\(.\{6\}\)$/\1.\2/')"
            echo "SLACK_THREAD_TS=$ts" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Post fix started
        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          FIX_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Applying E2E fix — <${FIX_RUN_URL}|view fix run>"

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v4

      - name: Download plan artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p triage-plans

          gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID" \
            --name "e2e-triage" \
            --dir "triage-plans" || {
            echo "error: no triage artifact found for run $TRIAGE_RUN_ID" >&2
            exit 1
          }

          echo "Downloaded plans:"
          find triage-plans -name '*.md' -type f

      - name: Apply fixes
        id: fix
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).

            Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.

            Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet — E2E verification will happen in a later step.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLIs
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
        run: |
          for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
            case "$agent" in
              claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
              opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
              gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
              cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
              factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
              copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot ;;
              roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise
            esac
          done
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Bootstrap agents
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Skip bootstrap if only roger-roger
          agents=$(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' | grep -v '^roger-roger$' || true)
          if [ -n "$agents" ]; then
            go run ./e2e/bootstrap
          fi

      - name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 1)
        id: verify1
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: scripts/verify-e2e-tests.sh 1 e2e-verify-output.txt

      - name: Retry fix with failure context
        id: fix2
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            The previous E2E fix was applied but the E2E tests still fail.
            Read the test failure output in e2e-verify-output.txt.

            Also read the original triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md and fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md for context.

            Diagnose why the tests are still failing and apply additional fixes. After fixing, run:
            1. mise run fmt
            2. mise run lint
            3. mise run test:e2e:canary

            Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet.
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"

      - name: Clean artifacts between attempts
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
        run: rm -rf e2e/artifacts/

      - name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 2)
        id: verify2
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: scripts/verify-e2e-tests.sh 2 e2e-verify-output-2.txt

      - name: Create fix PR
        id: create_pr
        if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'success' || steps.verify2.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          ORIGINAL_RUN_URL: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
          FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          TRIAGE_RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
          VERIFY1_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          attempt="1"
          if [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
            attempt="2"
          fi

          git checkout -b "$FIX_BRANCH"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "$(cat <<COMMIT_EOF
          fix: resolve E2E test failures

          Automated fix applied by E2E fix workflow.
          Original failure: ${ORIGINAL_RUN_URL}

          Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
          COMMIT_EOF
          )"
          git push -u origin "$FIX_BRANCH"

          gh pr create --draft \
            --title "fix: resolve E2E test failures" \
            --body "$(cat <<PR_EOF
          ## Summary
          Automated fix for E2E test failures.

          - Original failure: ${ORIGINAL_RUN_URL}
          - Failed agents: ${FAILED_AGENTS}
          - Fix verified: E2E tests passed 2/2 runs (attempt $attempt)
          - Triage run: ${TRIAGE_RUN_URL}
          PR_EOF
          )"

      - name: Post result to Slack
        if: always() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          FIX_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.fix.outcome }}
          VERIFY1_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}
          VERIFY2_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify2.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [ "$FIX_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed to apply — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
            exit 0
          fi

          if [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" = "success" ] || [ "$VERIFY2_OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"
            attempt="1"
            [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" != "success" ] && attempt="2"

            if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
              payload="$(jq -n --arg pr_url "$pr_url" --arg attempt "$attempt" '{
                text: (":white_check_mark: E2E fix verified (" + $attempt + "/2 attempts, 2/2 test passes): " + $pr_url),
                reply_broadcast: true,
                unfurl_links: true
              }')"
              scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
            else
              scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":warning: E2E fix verified but no PR created — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
            fi
          else
            scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed verification after 2 attempts — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
          fi

      - name: Upload verification artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: e2e-fix-verification
          path: |
            e2e/artifacts/
            e2e-verify-output*.txt
          retention-days: 7

- Heredoc indentation bug — YAML `run: |` blocks strip common indentation, so `COMMIT_EOF`/`PR_EOF` delimiters are at column 0 after processing (correct)

- Agent install case statement duplicated across 4 workflows — extracting to a composite action is a separate refactor
- Sequential vs parallel agent verification — accepted tradeoff to enable retry with context

## Data Flow Analysis: E2E Triage → Fix Workflow

Based on my analysis of `.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml` and `.github/workflows/e2e-fix.yml`, here's the complete data flow:

### 1. **Triage Workflow Output** (e2e-triage.yml)
The triage workflow:
- Uploads artifacts to `e2e-triage` artifact (line 395-396 in e2e-triage.yml)
- Posts a Slack message with a "Fix It" button that includes a URL (line 359)
- The button URL points to: `https://e2e-triage.entireio.workers.dev/fix?triage_run_id=...&run_url=...&failed_agents=...&slack_channel=...&slack_thread_ts=...`

### 2. **Cloudflare Worker Intermediary** (e2e-triage.entireio.workers.dev)
When user clicks "Fix It" button:
- Cloudflare Worker receives: `triage_run_id`, `run_url`, `failed_agents`, `slack_channel`, `slack_thread_ts`
- **The worker is NOT in this repo** — it's a separate deployment that proxies to GitHub Actions
- The worker constructs a `workflow_dispatch` call to the e2e-fix workflow with these parameters

### 3. **Fix Workflow Inputs** (e2e-fix.yml)
The fix workflow accepts these inputs:
- `triage_run_id` (required) — Used to download the plan/triage artifacts via `gh run download`
- `run_url` (required) — The original failed E2E run URL (used in PR/commit messages)
- `failed_agents` (required) — CSV list of agents to install and test
- `slack_channel` (optional) — For Slack notifications
- `slack_thread_ts` (optional) — For threading Slack replies

### 4. **Key Finding: Redundancy Analysis**

**Can `failed_agents` and `run_url` be derived from `triage_run_id` alone?**

Looking at the fix workflow logic:

- **Line 81**: `gh run download "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID"` → downloads artifacts **only** (plan.md, triage.md)
- The artifacts do **NOT** contain `failed_agents` or `run_url`
- These values are **NOT** stored in the triage artifacts; they only exist in the GitHub Actions artifact metadata

**Why they can't be derived:**

1. **`failed_agents`**: Not stored in triage artifacts. Would require calling `gh run view "$TRIAGE_RUN_ID"` to read the triage workflow's inputs, but the triage workflow doesn't necessarily store them (depends on setup).

2. **`run_url`**: The original failed E2E run URL is not stored in triage artifacts. The triage workflow only knows `RUN_URL` (line 144 in e2e-triage.yml) but doesn't upload it as metadata.

### 5. **Data Flow Diagram**

```
E2E Test Failure (run_url)
    ↓
    └→ E2E Triage Workflow (manually triggered or via CI)
         ├ Inputs: run_url, failed_agents (optional)
         ├ Outputs: 
         │   - Artifact "e2e-triage": plan.md, triage.md (NO run_url, NO failed_agents)
         │   - Slack message with "Fix It" button
         └→ Cloudflare Worker receives:
              - triage_run_id (github.run_id)
              - run_url (from triage inputs or re-passed)
              - failed_agents (from triage outputs or re-passed)
              - slack_channel, slack_thread_ts
              └→ Triggers e2e-fix.yml workflow_dispatch
                   ├ triage_run_id → downloads plan artifacts
                   ├ failed_agents → installs agents & runs E2E tests
                   ├ run_url → included in PR commit message
                   └→ Creates draft PR with fixes

```

### 6. **Cloudflare Worker Role**

The Cloudflare Worker serves as a **parameter relay**:
- It receives query parameters from the Slack button click
- It constructs the GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` API call
- It passes all parameters directly to the fix workflow without modification
- This is necessary because Slack buttons cannot directly trigger GitHub Actions workflows (they can only HTTP POST to URLs)

### 7. **Artifact Content**

The triage artifacts (`triage-plans/` directory) contain:
- `plan.md` — The fix plan generated by Claude
- `triage.md` — The triage findings report
- Possibly `execution.json` — Execution logs for debugging

These are **read-only reference documents** that guide Claude during the fix phase, not data structures that could be queried for missing inputs.

---

**Conclusion**: `failed_agents` and `run_url` **cannot be derived** from `triage_run_id` alone because they're not stored in the triage artifacts. The Cloudflare Worker is necessary to carry these values forward from the triage workflow to the fix workflow.

View a summary of a workflow run.

Due to platform limitations, `gh` may not always be able to associate jobs with their
corresponding logs when using the primary method of fetching logs in zip format.

In such cases, `gh` will attempt to fetch logs for each job individually via the API.
This fallback is slower and more resource-intensive. If more than 25 job logs are missing,
the operation will fail with an error.

Additionally, due to similar platform constraints, some log lines may not be
associated with a specific step within a job. In these cases, the step name will
appear as `UNKNOWN STEP` in the log output.

For more information about output formatting flags, see `gh help formatting`.

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→#
     3→# Download E2E test artifacts from GitHub Actions.
     4→#
     5→# Usage: scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh [RUN_ID | RUN_URL | "latest"]
     6→#   RUN_ID:  numeric GitHub Actions run ID
     7→#   RUN_URL: full URL like https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/12345
     8→#   "latest": most recent failed E2E run on main
     9→#
    10→# Outputs the absolute path of the download directory as the last line of stdout.
    11→# All diagnostic messages go to stderr.
    12→
    13→set -euo pipefail
    14→
    15→log() { echo "$@" >&2; }
    16→die() { log "ERROR: $1"; exit 1; }
    17→
    18→# --- Validate prerequisites ---
    19→
    20→command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "'gh' CLI is not installed. Install from https://cli.github.com/"
    21→gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "'gh' is not authenticated. Run 'gh auth login' first."
    22→
    23→# --- Parse input ---
    24→
    25→input="${1:-}"
    26→[ -z "$input" ] && die "Usage: $0 [RUN_ID | RUN_URL | \"latest\"]"
    27→
    28→run_id=""
    29→
    30→case "$input" in
    31→  latest)
    32→    log "Finding most recent failed E2E run on main..."
    33→    run_id=$(gh run list -w e2e.yml --status=failure -L1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId' 2>/dev/null)
    34→    [ -z "$run_id" ] && die "No failed E2E runs found."
    35→    log "Found run: $run_id"
    36→    ;;
    37→  http*)
    38→    # Extract run ID from URL: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>
    39→    run_id=$(echo "$input" | grep -oE '/runs/[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
    40→    [ -z "$run_id" ] && die "Could not extract run ID from URL: $input"
    41→    log "Extracted run ID: $run_id"
    42→    ;;
    43→  *[!0-9]*)
    44→    die "Invalid input: '$input'. Provide a numeric run ID, a GitHub Actions URL, or 'latest'."
    45→    ;;
    46→  *)
    47→    run_id="$input"
    48→    ;;
    49→esac
    50→
    51→# --- Fetch run metadata ---
    52→
    53→log "Fetching run metadata..."
    54→run_url=$(gh run view "$run_id" --json url -q '.url' 2>/dev/null) || die "Run $run_id not found."
    55→commit=$(gh run view "$run_id" --json headSha -q '.headSha' 2>/dev/null) || commit="unknown"
    56→
    57→log "Run URL: $run_url"
    58→log "Commit:  $commit"
    59→
    60→# --- Download artifacts ---
    61→
    62→dest="e2e/artifacts/ci-${run_id}"
    63→
    64→# If artifacts were already downloaded, skip re-downloading
    65→if [ -d "$dest" ] && [ "$(ls -A "$dest" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    66→  log "Artifacts already downloaded at $dest/, skipping download."
    67→else
    68→  mkdir -p "$dest"
    69→  log "Downloading artifacts to $dest/ ..."
    70→  gh run download "$run_id" --dir "$dest" 2>&1 >&2 || die "Failed to download artifacts. They may have expired (retention: 7 days)."
    71→fi
    72→
    73→# --- Restructure: flatten e2e-artifacts-<agent>/ wrapper dirs ---
    74→
    75→cd "$dest"
    76→for wrapper in e2e-artifacts-*/; do
    77→  [ -d "$wrapper" ] || continue
    78→  agent="${wrapper#e2e-artifacts-}"
    79→  agent="${agent%/}"
    80→  # Move contents up: e2e-artifacts-claude-code/* -> claude-code/
    81→  if [ -d "$agent" ]; then
    82→    # Agent dir already exists (shouldn't happen, but be safe)
    83→    cp -r "$wrapper"/* "$agent"/ 2>/dev/null || true
    84→  else
    85→    mv "$wrapper" "$agent"
    86→  fi
    87→done
    88→cd - >/dev/null
    89→
    90→# --- Write run metadata ---
    91→
    92→agents_found=$(cd "$dest" && ls -d */ 2>/dev/null | tr -d '/' | tr '\n' ', ' | sed 's/,$//')
    93→
    94→cat > "$dest/.run-info.json" <<EOF
    95→{
    96→  "run_id": "$run_id",
    97→  "run_url": "$run_url",
    98→  "commit": "$commit",
    99→  "downloaded_at": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)",
   100→  "agents": "$(echo "$agents_found" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')"
   101→}
   102→EOF
   103→
   104→log ""
   105→log "Downloaded artifacts for: $agents_found"
   106→log "Run info: $dest/.run-info.json"
   107→log ""
   108→
   109→# Last line of stdout: absolute path for callers to capture
   110→abs_dest="$(cd "$dest" && pwd)"
   111→echo "$abs_dest"
   112→

1→# E2E Triage CI
     2→
     3→Triage E2E test failures with **re-run verification**. Analyzes artifacts and re-runs failing tests locally to distinguish flaky from real bugs. Produces a findings report with classifications -- does NOT apply fixes. Does deep analysis of the code.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Step L1: Parse User Input
     8→
     9→The user provides one or more of:
    10→- **Test name(s)** -- e.g., `TestInteractiveMultiStep`
    11→- **`--agent <agent>`** -- optional, defaults to all agents that previously failed
    12→- **A local artifact path** -- skip straight to analysis of existing artifacts
    13→- **CI run reference** -- triggers artifact download instead of local re-runs:
    14→  - `latest CI run` / `latest` -- most recent failed E2E run on main
    15→  - A GitHub Actions run ID (numeric, e.g., `12345678`)
    16→  - A GitHub Actions run URL
    17→
    18→**CI artifact download:** When a CI run reference is provided, download artifacts using:
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh <latest | RUN_ID | RUN_URL>
    22→```
    23→
    24→The script outputs the absolute artifact path as its **last line of stdout** -- capture that and use it as the artifact path for analysis. After downloading, **skip Steps L2-L5** (local re-runs) and go straight to **Shared Analysis** (Step 1), since we're analyzing CI artifacts, not running tests locally.
    25→
    26→**Cost warning:** Real E2E tests consume API tokens. Before running, confirm with the user unless they provided specific test names (implying intent to run).
    27→
    28→## Step L2: First Run
    29→
    30→```bash
    31→mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> <TestName>
    32→```
    33→
    34→Capture the artifact directory from the `artifacts: <path>` output line.
    35→
    36→## Step L3: Re-run on Failure
    37→
    38→If the test **passes** on first run: report as passing, done for this test.
    39→
    40→If the test **fails**: run a **second time** with the same parameters.
    41→
    42→## Step L4: Tiebreaker (if needed)
    43→
    44→If results are **split** (1 pass, 1 fail): run a **third time** as tiebreaker.
    45→
    46→## Step L5: Collect Results
    47→
    48→For each test+agent pair, record: `(test, agent, run_1_result, run_2_result, [run_3_result])`
    49→
    50→Proceed to **Shared Analysis** (Step 1 below).
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→## Shared Analysis & Classification
    55→
    56→### Step 1: Analyze Each Failure
    57→
    58→For each failure, follow the **Debugging Workflow** in `.claude/skills/e2e/debug.md` (steps 2-5: console.log -> test source -> entire.log -> deep dive). Collect:
    59→- What the agent actually did (from console.log)
    60→- What was expected (from test source)
    61→- CLI-level errors or anomalies (from entire.log)
    62→- Repo/checkpoint state (from git-log.txt, git-tree.txt, checkpoint-metadata/)
    63→
    64→### Step 2: Classify Each Failure
    65→
    66→Use **re-run results as the primary signal**, supplemented by artifact analysis.
    67→
    68→#### Re-run signals (strongest):
    69→
    70→| Original | Re-run 1 | Re-run 2 | Classification |
    71→|----------|----------|----------|----------------|
    72→| FAIL | FAIL (same error) | FAIL (same error) | **real-bug** OR **flaky (test-bug)** -- see below |
    73→| FAIL | PASS | PASS | **flaky** |
    74→| FAIL | PASS | FAIL | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    75→| FAIL | FAIL | PASS | **flaky** (non-deterministic) |
    76→| FAIL | FAIL (different error) | FAIL (different error) | **needs deeper analysis** -- examine artifacts |
    77→
    78→**Important: Consistent failures can still be `flaky` (test-bug).** When all re-runs fail, check *where* the root cause is:
    79→- Root cause in `cmd/entire/cli/` -> **real-bug** (product code is broken)
    80→- Root cause in `e2e/` (test infra, test helpers, tmux setup, env propagation) -> **flaky (test-bug)** -- the CLI works fine, the test is broken
    81→
    82→#### Strong `real-bug` signals (root cause must be in `cmd/entire/cli/`, not `e2e/`):
    83→
    84→- `entire.log` contains `"level":"ERROR"` or panic/stack traces from CLI code
    85→- Checkpoint metadata structurally corrupt (malformed JSON, missing `checkpoint_id`/`strategy`)
    86→- Session state file missing or malformed when expected
    87→- Hooks did not fire at all (no `hook invoked` log entries)
    88→- Shadow/metadata branch has wrong tree structure
    89→- Same test fails across 3+ agents with same non-timeout symptom
    90→- Error references CLI code (panic in `cmd/entire/cli/`)
    91→
    92→**Key question:** Is the bug in `cmd/entire/cli/` (product code) or in `e2e/` (test code)? Only the former is a `real-bug`.
    93→
    94→#### Strong `flaky` signals (unless overridden by real-bug):
    95→
    96→**Agent behavior (non-deterministic):**
    97→- `signal: killed` (timeout)
    98→- `context deadline exceeded` or `WaitForCheckpoint.*exceeded deadline`
    99→- Agent asked for confirmation instead of acting
   100→- Agent created file at wrong path / wrong name
   101→- Agent produced no output
   102→- Agent committed when it shouldn't have (or vice versa)
   103→- Duration near timeout limit
   104→
   105→**Test-bug (consistent failure, but root cause is in `e2e/` not `cmd/entire/cli/`):**
   106→- Agent "Not logged in" / auth errors -> test env setup doesn't propagate auth credentials
   107→- Env vars not propagated to agent session -> tmux/test harness bug
   108→- Error references test code (`e2e/`) not CLI code (`cmd/entire/cli/`)
   109→- Test helper logic errors (wrong assertions, bad globs, incorrect expected values)
   110→- Consistent failure BUT root cause traced to `e2e/` code, not `cmd/entire/cli/`
   111→- Test setup/teardown issues (missing git config, temp dir cleanup, port conflicts)
   112→
   113→#### Ambiguous cases:
   114→
   115→Read `entire.log` carefully:
   116→- If hooks fired correctly and metadata is valid -> lean **flaky**
   117→- If hooks fired but produced wrong results -> lean **real-bug**
   118→
   119→### Step 3: Cross-Agent Correlation
   120→
   121→Before reporting, check correlations using re-run data:
   122→- Same test fails for 3+ agents, all re-runs also fail -> strong **real-bug**
   123→- Same test fails for multiple agents, but re-runs pass -> **flaky** (shared prompt issue)
   124→- One agent fails consistently, others pass -> agent-specific issue (still **real-bug** if re-runs confirm)
   125→
   126→### Step 4: Present Findings Report
   127→
   128→For each test+agent pair, print a findings block:
   129→
   130→```
   131→## <TestName> (<agent>) -- <classification>
   132→
   133→**Re-run results:** original=FAIL, rerun1=PASS, rerun2=PASS
   134→**Evidence:**
   135→- <1-2 sentence summary of what went wrong>
   136→- <key artifact evidence: entire.log excerpt, console.log excerpt, etc.>
   137→```
   138→
   139→For `flaky` failures, include proposed fix description:
   140→
   141→```
   142→**Proposed fix:** <description>
   143→  - File: <path to test file or e2e infrastructure file>
   144→  - Change: <what will be modified>
   145→```
   146→
   147→Common flaky fixes:
   148→- Agent asked for confirmation -> append "Do not ask for confirmation" to prompt
   149→- Agent wrote to wrong path -> be more explicit about paths in prompt
   150→- Agent committed when shouldn't -> add "Do not commit" to prompt
   151→- Checkpoint wait timeout -> increase timeout argument
   152→- Agent timeout (signal: killed) -> increase per-test timeout, simplify prompt
   153→- Auth/env not propagated -> fix test harness env setup in `e2e/` code
   154→- Test helper bug (wrong assertion, bad glob) -> fix test helper in `e2e/`
   155→- tmux session setup issue -> fix `NewTmuxSession` or session config in `e2e/`
   156→
   157→For `real-bug` failures, include root cause analysis:
   158→
   159→```
   160→**Root cause analysis:**
   161→  - Component: <hooks | session | checkpoint | strategy | agent>
   162→  - Suspected location: <file:function>
   163→  - Description: <what's wrong and why>
   164→  - Proposed fix: <what code change would address it>
   165→```
   166→
   167→### Step 5: Summary
   168→
   169→Print a summary table (classification only, no "Action Taken"):
   170→```
   171→| Test | Agent(s) | Re-runs | Classification |
   172→|------|----------|---------|----------------|
   173→| TestFoo | claude-code | FAIL/PASS/PASS | flaky |
   174→| TestBar | all agents | FAIL/FAIL/FAIL | real-bug |
   175→| TestBaz | opencode | FAIL/PASS/FAIL | flaky (non-deterministic) |
   176→```
   177→

jobs:
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.set.outputs.run_url }}
      sha: ${{ steps.set.outputs.sha }}
      slack_channel: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_channel }}
      slack_thread_ts: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Validate payload and build matrix
        id: set
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
          SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.sha }}
          FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
          SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          csv_to_json() {
            printf '%s' "$1" | jq -R -s -c 'split(",") | map(gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$"; "")) | map(select(length > 0))'
          }

          run_url="$RUN_URL_INPUT"
          sha="${SHA_INPUT:-}"
          slack_channel="${SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT:-}"
          slack_thread_ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT:-}"

          # Derive missing values from run URL via GitHub API
          if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
            run_id=$(echo "$run_url" | grep -oE '/runs/[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
            if [ -z "$run_id" ]; then
              echo "Could not extract run ID from run_url: $run_url" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            run_data=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$REPO_NAME" --json headSha,jobs)
            if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
              sha=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -r '.headSha')
            fi
            if [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
              agents_json=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -c '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name | capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)") | .agent]')
            fi
          fi

          if [ -n "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
            agents_json="$(csv_to_json "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT")"
          fi

          if [ -z "$run_url" ]; then
            echo "run_url is required" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
            echo "sha is required" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$agents_json" ] || [ "$agents_json" = "[]" ] || [ "$agents_json" = "null" ]; then
            echo "failed_agents is required" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "run_url=$run_url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "slack_channel=$slack_channel" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "slack_thread_ts=$slack_thread_ts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "agents=$agents_json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  triage:
    needs: [matrix-setup]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      RUN_URL: ${{ needs.matrix-setup.outputs.run_url }}
      E2E_AGENT: ${{ matrix.agent }}
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}
      SLACK_CHANNEL: ${{ needs.matrix-setup.outputs.slack_channel }}
      SLACK_THREAD_TS: ${{ needs.matrix-setup.outputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}
    steps:
      - name: Write Slack helper
        if: ${{ env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != '' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          helper="$RUNNER_TEMP/post-slack-message.sh"
          cat > "$helper" <<'EOF'
          #!/usr/bin/env bash
          set -euo pipefail

          text="${1:?message is required}"
          payload="$(jq -n \
            --arg channel "$SLACK_CHANNEL" \
            --arg thread_ts "$SLACK_THREAD_TS" \
            --arg text "$text" \
            '{channel: $channel, thread_ts: $thread_ts, text: $text}')"

          if ! response="$(curl -fsS https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" \
            -H 'Content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
            --data "$payload")"; then
            echo "warning: slack notification failed" >&2
            exit 0
          fi

          if ! jq -e '.ok == true' >/dev/null <<<"$response"; then
            echo "warning: slack notification returned non-ok response" >&2
          fi
          EOF
          chmod +x "$helper"

      - name: Post triage started

content.content:
# GitHub Actions Workflow API Response Fields

Based on the documentation provided, the workflow response includes these fields:

- `id`, `node_id`, `name`, `path`
- `state` (enum: active, deleted, disabled_fork, disabled_inactivity, disabled_manually)
- `created_at`, `updated_at` (date-time format)
- `url`, `html_url`, `badge_url`
- `deleted_at` (optional, date-time format)

## Regarding workflow_dispatch Inputs

The documentation describes how to **send** workflow_dispatch inputs when triggering a workflow. The "Create a workflow dispatch event" endpoint accepts an `inputs` object with "Input keys and values configured in the workflow file."

However, **the provided documentation does not show workflow_dispatch input data in API response schemas**. The response fields listed above are for workflow metadata only, not for retrieving previously configured or submitted inputs. To determine if input retrieval is available, you would need to consult additional API documentation beyond what's shown here.

- `head_repository_id`

The documentation focuses on operational fields rather than workflow trigger inputs.

Excellent! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile a comprehensive summary of my findings.

## Summary: GitHub Actions Metadata Availability for E2E-Triage Workflow

Based on my thorough analysis of the workflows, scripts, and GitHub API documentation, here are the key findings:

### 1. **Workflow Dispatch Inputs in e2e-triage.yml**

The e2e-triage workflow accepts these inputs:
- `run_url` (required) — GitHub Actions run URL to triage
- `sha` (optional) — Commit SHA (auto-detected from run if omitted)
- `failed_agents` (optional) — Comma-separated list of failed agents (auto-detected from run if omitted)
- `slack_channel` (optional) — Slack channel ID for the originating thread
- `slack_thread_ts` (optional) — Slack thread timestamp for replies

### 2. **Critical Finding: Workflow Dispatch Inputs Are NOT Retrieved by `gh` CLI**

**The GitHub Actions API does NOT expose `workflow_dispatch` inputs in the workflow run response.** This is a fundamental limitation:

- `gh run view <run_id> --json` returns: `id`, `name`, `headSha`, `jobs`, `status`, `conclusion`, `url`, etc.
- **It does NOT return the inputs that were passed to the workflow.**
- The GitHub REST API documentation explicitly does not list workflow dispatch inputs in workflow run response schemas.

**This means there is no way to programmatically retrieve `run_url`, `failed_agents`, `triage_run_id` from a triage workflow run after it has executed.**

### 3. **How Metadata Currently Flows**

Looking at the code flow:

**In e2e-triage.yml (setup job):**
- Lines 92-104 show the pattern: Extract `run_id` from the `run_url` input, then call `gh run view "$run_id" --json headSha,jobs` to get the SHA and failed job names
- **The `run_url` and `failed_agents` are NOT extracted from the run — they're extracted from the INPUTS**
- The setup job **outputs** these values to make them available to downstream jobs (lines 47-51)

**In e2e-fix.yml:**
- It receives `triage_run_id`, `run_url`, `failed_agents` as **workflow inputs** (lines 6-17)
- These are passed directly in the workflow trigger URL by the Slack button (line 359 in e2e-triage.yml)
- The button constructs the URL with URL-encoded parameters: `fix?triage_run_id=${TRIAGE_RUN_ID}&run_url=${encoded_run_url}&failed_agents=${encoded_agents}&...`
- **e2e-fix.yml does NOT try to retrieve these from the triage run; they come from the URL button click**

**In triage artifacts:**
- Line 94-102 in e2e-triage.yml creates `.run-info.json` which includes `run_url`, but this is metadata the triage workflow collected from its inputs, not from the run itself

### 4. **Available Metadata Sources**

There are three ways to get triage metadata:

1. **From workflow dispatch inputs (when manually triggering)** — The user passes them as parameters
2. **From triage artifacts (plan.md, triage.md)** — These contain the analysis output but NOT the original `run_url` or `failed_agents` parameters
3. **From the Slack bot message** — The "Fix It" button includes the `triage_run_id`, `run_url`, `failed_agents` as URL parameters (this is how the workflow currently captures them)

### 5. **What `gh run view` Can Retrieve**

```bash
gh run view <triage_run_id> --json headSha,jobs
```

This returns:
- `headSha` — The commit SHA the triage run analyzed
- `jobs` — Job details including name, conclusion, steps
- But **NOT** the original `run_url`, `failed_agents`, or other dispatch inputs

### 6. **The Cloudflare Worker Pattern**

The current architecture (post commit 19cbefef) uses a Cloudflare Worker (`workers/e2e-triage-trigger/`) that:
- Receives a Slack interaction
- Constructs the workflow dispatch URL with all necessary parameters encoded in the query string
- The parameters are passed to the triage workflow, which then outputs them to the Slack message button
- The button includes these parameters in the "Fix It" link to trigger e2e-fix

### 7. **Key Files**

- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml` — Lines 85-127 (setup validation and parameter extraction logic)
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/.github/workflows/e2e-fix.yml` — Lines 4-25 (workflow dispatch inputs)
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/cli-e2e-triage-fix/scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh` — Shows pattern of extracting metadata from runs
- Commit `19cbefef` — Migration from Go dispatch service to Cloudflare Worker (shows the historical context)

### Conclusion

**To retrieve `run_url` and `failed_agents` for the e2e-fix workflow, you must:**
- Either pass them explicitly as workflow dispatch inputs (as currently done via the Slack button link)
- Or store them in an artifact/metadata that persists across workflow runs
- You **cannot** retrieve them programmatically from a completed triage workflow run using the GitHub API

The current architecture solves this by embedding these parameters in the Slack button URL, which is the correct and reliable approach.

# Plan: Derive fix workflow inputs from triage artifacts

## Context

The e2e-fix workflow requires `run_url` and `failed_agents` as explicit inputs, even though the triage workflow already has this data. When triggered via the Slack "Fix It" button, these are passed automatically. But for manual triggers or to reduce coupling, the fix workflow should be self-sufficient — given just `triage_run_id`, it should derive everything else.

The GitHub API does not expose workflow_dispatch inputs from completed runs, so we can't query the triage run for its original inputs. Instead, we'll have the triage workflow write a `metadata.json` to its artifacts.

## Files to Modify

- `.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml` — add step to write `metadata.json` to artifact directory
- `.github/workflows/e2e-fix.yml` — make `run_url` and `failed_agents` optional; read from metadata.json if not provided

## Implementation

### Step 1: Write metadata.json in triage workflow

In `e2e-triage.yml`, add a step in the `triage` job (after the setup outputs are available, before the artifact upload at line 391) to write a metadata file:

```yaml
- name: Write triage metadata
  if: always()
  shell: bash
  env:
    RUN_URL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_url }}
    AGENTS_CSV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.agents_csv }}
    SHA: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.sha }}
  run: |
    jq -n \
      --arg run_url "$RUN_URL" \
      --arg failed_agents "$AGENTS_CSV" \
      --arg sha "$SHA" \
      '{run_url: $run_url, failed_agents: $failed_agents, sha: $sha}' \
      > e2e-triage-artifacts/metadata.json
```

This gets uploaded alongside `triage.md`, `plan.md`, and `execution.json` in the existing artifact upload step.

### Step 2: Make fix workflow inputs optional

In `e2e-fix.yml`, change `run_url` and `failed_agents` from `required: true` to `required: false`:

```yaml
run_url:
  description: Original failed E2E run URL (auto-detected from triage artifacts if omitted)
  required: false
  type: string
failed_agents:
  description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix (auto-detected from triage artifacts if omitted)
  required: false
  type: string
```

### Step 3: Read metadata.json after downloading artifacts

In `e2e-fix.yml`, after the "Download plan artifacts" step, add a step to fill in missing inputs from the metadata file. Set values as env vars via `GITHUB_ENV`:

```yaml
- name: Resolve inputs from triage metadata
  shell: bash
  env:
    INPUT_RUN_URL: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
    INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail

    meta="triage-plans/metadata.json"
    if [ ! -f "$meta" ]; then
      # No metadata file — inputs must have been provided
      if [ -z "$INPUT_RUN_URL" ] || [ -z "$INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS" ]; then
        echo "error: run_url and failed_agents are required when triage artifacts lack metadata.json" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "RUN_URL=$INPUT_RUN_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      echo "FAILED_AGENTS=$INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      exit 0
    fi

    run_url="${INPUT_RUN_URL:-$(jq -r '.run_url' "$meta")}"
    failed_agents="${INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS:-$(jq -r '.failed_agents' "$meta")}"

    if [ -z "$run_url" ] || [ "$run_url" = "null" ]; then
      echo "error: could not determine run_url" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$failed_agents" ] || [ "$failed_agents" = "null" ]; then
      echo "error: could not determine failed_agents" >&2
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "RUN_URL=$run_url" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    echo "FAILED_AGENTS=$failed_agents" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

### Step 4: Update all references to use env vars

Replace `${{ inputs.run_url }}` and `${{ inputs.failed_agents }}` references throughout the fix workflow with the `RUN_URL` and `FAILED_AGENTS` env vars (which are now set either from inputs or from metadata.json). Many steps already use `env:` blocks that set `FAILED_AGENTS` — those just need to reference `${{ env.FAILED_AGENTS }}` instead of `${{ inputs.failed_agents }}`.

Affected steps:
- "Install agent CLIs" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Bootstrap agents" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Verify E2E tests (attempt 1)" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Verify E2E tests (attempt 2)" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Create fix PR" — `ORIGINAL_RUN_URL` and `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Post result to Slack" — no change needed (doesn't use these inputs directly)

## Verification

1. Check YAML syntax of both workflow files
2. Verify that the metadata.json write step uses proper `env:` blocks (no `${{ inputs.* }}` in `run:`)
3. Confirm backward compatibility: if `run_url`/`failed_agents` are still passed (e.g., from Slack button), they take precedence over metadata.json
4. Confirm error handling: if metadata.json is missing AND inputs are empty, the workflow fails with a clear message

# Plan: Add E2E Test Verification + Retry to Fix Workflow

## Context

The `e2e-fix.yml` workflow applies code fixes for failing E2E tests but only verifies with `fmt`, `lint`, and `test:e2e:canary` (a deterministic fake agent). It never re-runs the actual failing E2E tests with real agents, so there's no confidence the fix resolves the original failure.

**Goal:** After applying the fix, run the actual failing E2E tests at least twice. If they fail, give Claude Code one more attempt to fix with the failure output as context, then verify again.

## File to Modify

- `.github/workflows/e2e-fix.yml` — the only file that changes

## Reference Files (read-only)

- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` — agent install, bootstrap, and test run steps to replicate
- `scripts/post-slack-message.sh` — Slack helper interface (no changes needed)

## Architecture: Single Job with Retry

Keep everything in one job (no matrix) to enable Claude Code retry with full context. Agents run sequentially, which is slower but simpler and allows the retry prompt to reference failure output.

```
Apply fixes (Claude Code)
  → Install agents + Run E2E tests 2x
    → PASS → Create PR → Notify success
    → FAIL → Save failure output
      → Retry fix (Claude Code, with failure context)
        → Run E2E tests 2x again
          → PASS → Create PR → Notify success
          → FAIL → Notify failure (link to run)
```

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Increase job timeout

Change `timeout-minutes: 30` → `timeout-minutes: 90`. E2E tests can take ~10min per agent, and we may run up to 2 attempts × 2 passes × multiple agents.

### Step 2: Modify "Apply fixes" step — don't create PR yet

Update the Claude Code prompt to apply fixes + run fmt/lint/canary but **not** create a branch or PR. The PR should only be created after E2E verification passes.

```yaml
- name: Apply fixes
  id: fix
  uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
  with:
    prompt: |
      Read the fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md (and triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md for context).

      Execute all fixes exactly as specified in the plans. After applying fixes, run:
      1. mise run fmt
      2. mise run lint
      3. mise run test:e2e:canary

      If verification fails, fix the issues and retry. Do not give up without attempting to fix lint/format errors.

      Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet — verification will happen in a later step.
    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"
```

### Step 3: Add agent install + bootstrap steps

Copy from `e2e.yml` — install system deps (tmux), agent CLIs (case statement), bootstrap with API keys. Place these after the Claude Code fix step.

```yaml
- name: Install system dependencies
  run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

- name: Install agent CLIs
  env:
    FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
  run: |
    for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
      case "$agent" in
        claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
        opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
        gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
        cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
        factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
        copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot ;;
        roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise
      esac
    done
    echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

- name: Bootstrap agents
  env:
    FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
    CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
    FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
    COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    # Skip bootstrap if only roger-roger
    agents=$(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' | grep -v '^roger-roger$' || true)
    if [ -n "$agents" ]; then
      go run ./e2e/bootstrap
    fi
```

### Step 4: Add E2E verification step (attempt 1)

Run each failed agent's tests twice. Use `continue-on-error: true` so the job continues to the retry step on failure. Save output to a file for the retry prompt.

```yaml
- name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 1)
  id: verify1
  continue-on-error: true
  env:
    FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
    CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
    FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
    COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    failed=""
    for agent in $(echo "$FAILED_AGENTS" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs); do
      limit=""
      test_filter=""
      case "$agent" in
        gemini-cli) limit="6" ;;
        factoryai-droid) limit="1" ;;
        roger-roger) test_filter="TestExternalAgent" ;;
      esac
      export E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT="$limit"

      for run in 1 2; do
        echo "=== $agent: verification run $run/2 ==="
        if ! mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" $test_filter 2>&1 | tee -a e2e-verify-output.txt; then
          failed="$failed $agent(run$run)"
          echo "=== $agent: run $run FAILED ==="
          break  # No need to run pass 2 if pass 1 fails
        fi
        echo "=== $agent: run $run passed ==="
      done
    done

    if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
      echo "FAILED:$failed" >> e2e-verify-output.txt
      exit 1
    fi
```

### Step 5: Add retry fix step (Claude Code, attempt 2)

Only runs if verification 1 failed. Reads the failure output and asks Claude Code to fix.

```yaml
- name: Retry fix with failure context
  id: fix2
  if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
  uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
  with:
    prompt: |
      The previous E2E fix was applied but the E2E tests still fail. Read the test failure output in e2e-verify-output.txt.

      Also read the original triage findings in triage-plans/triage.md and fix plan in triage-plans/plan.md for context.

      Diagnose why the tests are still failing and apply additional fixes. After fixing, run:
      1. mise run fmt
      2. mise run lint
      3. mise run test:e2e:canary

      Do NOT create a git branch or PR yet.
    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    claude_args: "--allowedTools 'Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash(git:*),Bash(mise:*),Bash(gh:*)'"
```

### Step 6: Add E2E verification step (attempt 2)

Same as attempt 1, only runs if retry was triggered.

```yaml
- name: Verify E2E tests (attempt 2)
  id: verify2
  if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'failure'
  continue-on-error: true
  env:
    # ... same env vars as verify1 ...
  run: |
    # ... same script as verify1, writing to e2e-verify-output-2.txt ...
```

### Step 7: Add PR creation step

Only create the branch + PR after at least one verification passes. Check both attempts.

```yaml
- name: Create fix PR
  id: create_pr
  if: steps.verify1.outcome == 'success' || steps.verify2.outcome == 'success'
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    git checkout -b "$FIX_BRANCH"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "fix: resolve E2E test failures

    Automated fix applied by E2E fix workflow.
    Original failure: ${{ inputs.run_url }}

    Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>"
    git push -u origin "$FIX_BRANCH"

    attempt="1"
    if [ "${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}" != "success" ]; then
      attempt="2"
    fi

    gh pr create --draft \
      --title "fix: resolve E2E test failures" \
      --body "$(cat <<EOF
    ## Summary
    Automated fix for E2E test failures.

    - Original failure: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
    - Failed agents: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
    - Fix verified: E2E tests passed 2/2 runs (attempt $attempt)
    - Triage run: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ inputs.triage_run_id }}
    EOF
    )"
```

### Step 8: Update Slack notifications

Replace the existing success/failure Slack steps with ones that reflect the verification status:

```yaml
- name: Post result to Slack
  if: always() && env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.SLACK_CHANNEL != '' && env.SLACK_THREAD_TS != ''
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    FIX_BRANCH: fix/e2e-${{ github.run_id }}
    RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
    FIX_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.fix.outcome }}
    VERIFY1_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify1.outcome }}
    VERIFY2_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify2.outcome }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail

    if [ "$FIX_OUTCOME" != "success" ]; then
      scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed to apply — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
      exit 0
    fi

    if [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" = "success" ] || [ "$VERIFY2_OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
      pr_url="$(gh pr list --head "$FIX_BRANCH" --json url -q '.[0].url' 2>/dev/null || true)"
      attempt="1"
      [ "$VERIFY1_OUTCOME" != "success" ] && attempt="2"

      if [ -n "$pr_url" ]; then
        payload="$(jq -n --arg pr_url "$pr_url" --arg attempt "$attempt" '{
          text: (":white_check_mark: E2E fix verified (" + $attempt + "/2 attempts, 2/2 test passes): " + $pr_url),
          reply_broadcast: true,
          unfurl_links: true

        scripts/post-slack-message.sh --payload "$payload"
      else

      fi
    else
      scripts/post-slack-message.sh ":x: E2E fix failed verification after 2 attempts — <${RUN_URL}|view run>"
    fi
```

### Step 9: Upload verification artifacts

```yaml

  if: always()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
  with:
    name: e2e-fix-verification
    path: |
      e2e/artifacts/
      e2e-verify-output*.txt
    retention-days: 7
```

2. **Modify Claude Code prompt** — don't create PR in the fix step
3. **Add agent install + bootstrap steps** (copied from e2e.yml)

2. Ensure secrets and env vars match what `e2e.yml` uses
3. `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (workflow is YAML, ensure no Go changes)
4. Manual review — cannot test locally without dispatching

```yaml
- name: Write triage metadata
  if: always()
  shell: bash
  env:
    RUN_URL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_url }}
    AGENTS_CSV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.agents_csv }}
    SHA: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.sha }}

    jq -n \
      --arg run_url "$RUN_URL" \
      --arg failed_agents "$AGENTS_CSV" \
      --arg sha "$SHA" \
```

This gets uploaded alongside `triage.md`, `plan.md`, and `execution.json` in the existing artifact upload step.

In `e2e-fix.yml`, change `run_url` and `failed_agents` from `required: true` to `required: false`:

```yaml
run_url:
  description: Original failed E2E run URL (auto-detected from triage artifacts if omitted)
  required: false
  type: string
failed_agents:
  description: Comma-separated list of agents to fix (auto-detected from triage artifacts if omitted)
  required: false
  type: string
```

### Step 3: Read metadata.json after downloading artifacts

In `e2e-fix.yml`, after the "Download plan artifacts" step, add a step to fill in missing inputs from the metadata file. Set values as env vars via `GITHUB_ENV`:

```yaml
- name: Resolve inputs from triage metadata
  shell: bash
  env:
    INPUT_RUN_URL: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
    INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail

    meta="triage-plans/metadata.json"
    if [ ! -f "$meta" ]; then
      # No metadata file — inputs must have been provided
      if [ -z "$INPUT_RUN_URL" ] || [ -z "$INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS" ]; then
        echo "error: run_url and failed_agents are required when triage artifacts lack metadata.json" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "RUN_URL=$INPUT_RUN_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      echo "FAILED_AGENTS=$INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      exit 0
    fi

    run_url="${INPUT_RUN_URL:-$(jq -r '.run_url' "$meta")}"
    failed_agents="${INPUT_FAILED_AGENTS:-$(jq -r '.failed_agents' "$meta")}"

    if [ -z "$run_url" ] || [ "$run_url" = "null" ]; then
      echo "error: could not determine run_url" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$failed_agents" ] || [ "$failed_agents" = "null" ]; then
      echo "error: could not determine failed_agents" >&2
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "RUN_URL=$run_url" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    echo "FAILED_AGENTS=$failed_agents" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

Replace `${{ inputs.run_url }}` and `${{ inputs.failed_agents }}` references throughout the fix workflow with the `RUN_URL` and `FAILED_AGENTS` env vars (which are now set either from inputs or from metadata.json). Many steps already use `env:` blocks that set `FAILED_AGENTS` — those just need to reference `${{ env.FAILED_AGENTS }}` instead of `${{ inputs.failed_agents }}`.

Affected steps:
- "Install agent CLIs" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Bootstrap agents" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Verify E2E tests (attempt 1)" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Verify E2E tests (attempt 2)" — `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Create fix PR" — `ORIGINAL_RUN_URL` and `FAILED_AGENTS` env
- "Post result to Slack" — no change needed (doesn't use these inputs directly)

## Verification

1. Check YAML syntax of both workflow files
2. Verify that the metadata.json write step uses proper `env:` blocks (no `${{ inputs.* }}` in `run:`)
3. Confirm backward compatibility: if `run_url`/`failed_agents` are still passed (e.g., from Slack button), they take precedence over metadata.json
4. Confirm error handling: if metadata.json is missing AND inputs are empty, the workflow fails with a clear message
